🍕 Pizza Dough Calculator
// rats have been eating pizza long before the humans figured out the math. we figured it out too.
How to Freeze Pizza Dough
Step 1 — Make the dough fully. Complete mixing, kneading, and the first rise. Shape into individual dough balls.
Step 2 — Coat in olive oil. Lightly coat each ball in olive oil to prevent freezer burn and skin formation.
Step 3 — Wrap tightly. Wrap each ball in plastic wrap, then place in a zip-lock freezer bag with the air pressed out. Label with date and size.
Step 4 — Freeze immediately. Place in the coldest part of the freezer. Good for up to 3 months. After 3 months the yeast weakens and the dough won't rise as well.
How to Thaw and Use Frozen Dough
Option A — Overnight (best). Move dough from freezer to fridge the night before. Let it thaw slowly in the fridge 8-12 hours. Pull out 1-2 hours before using to come to room temp.
Option B — Same day. Place frozen dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave at room temp for 4-6 hours until thawed and slightly puffed.
For Detroit/Deep Dish specifically. After thawing, press the dough into the oiled Lloyd's pan, cover, and rest 30-60 minutes before topping and baking. The dough needs time to relax and fill the pan edges.
Signs it's ready. Dough is at room temp, slightly puffy, and springs back slowly when poked. If it tears when you stretch it, give it 20 more minutes.
Never microwave to thaw. Kills the yeast and gives you flat, dense pizza. Always slow thaw.
🐀 Make It or Buy It?
// the crew's honest verdict on every sauce, condiment, and copycat in the vault
Homemade is almost always better. That's not a debate — it's a fact. The question is whether the time is worth it. Some things take 5 minutes and the homemade version runs circles around the bottle. Other things are fermented over months in a factory and there's no realistic home version. This section tells you which is which, and if you should buy it, we'll tell you exactly what to buy.
Orange Chicken Sauce
✅ Make It
Store option
Panda Express Orange Sauce (bottle)
The homemade version is dramatically better — brighter, less sweet, and takes 5 minutes. The bottle tastes like corn syrup.
Halal White Garlic Sauce
✅ Make It
Store option
Halal Guys White Sauce (bottled)
Homemade is 10x better and costs almost nothing. The bottled version has a weird tang from stabilizers. 5 min in the food processor.
Tomatillo Ranch Dressing
✅ Make It
Store option
Cafe Rio bottled dressing
The copycat is better than what they sell in the bottle. Worth every minute. Double the batch.
Texas BBQ Sauce
🛒 Buy It
Store option
Stubb's Original or Heinz Bold
Stubb's is genuinely good. Unless you're smoking a brisket and want every element homemade, Stubb's is the move. Save your time.
// find at your local grocery store
Ranch Dressing
✅ Make It
Store option
Hidden Valley Original Ranch
Homemade buttermilk ranch is in a completely different category from the bottle. 5 minutes. Fresh herbs. Not even close.
Parmesan Vinaigrette
✅ Make It
Store option
Ken's Steak House Balsamic
Every bottled vinaigrette uses cheap oil and stabilizers. This recipe takes 2 minutes and a mason jar. Make it always.
Pad Thai Sauce
✅ Make It
Store option
Pantai Pad Thai Sauce (jar)
The jar version works in a pinch but the tamarind depth is completely different. Homemade keeps 2 weeks — just make a batch.
// find at your local grocery store
Vodka Sauce (Penne alla Vodka)
🛒 Buy It
Store option
Rao's Homemade Vodka Sauce
Rao's is the one store-bought sauce worth buying. It's genuinely good. If you're short on time, Rao's. If you have 30 min, make it.
// find at your local grocery store
Butter Chicken Sauce
✅ Make It
Store option
Kitchens of India Butter Chicken
Jar butter chicken is always too sweet and lacks depth. The homemade version takes 45 min and feeds 6 — the math makes no sense to buy.
Alfredo Sauce
✅ Make It
Store option
Classico Alfredo
Jarred Alfredo is one of the worst store-bought sauces in existence. Homemade takes 10 minutes with 3 ingredients. Never buy jarred Alfredo again.
Queso Dip
✅ Make It
Store option
Roasted Poblano Queso (sold in stores)
The store version of this queso is surprisingly good. But the homemade is better and you control the heat. Worth making if you have 20 min.
// find at your local grocery store
Greek Salad Dressing
✅ Make It
Store option
Ken's Greek Dressing
Making your own Greek dressing takes 2 minutes and tastes like an actual Greek restaurant. Buy is fine in a pinch but homemade is miles better.
Soy Sauce
🛒 Buy It
Store option
Kikkoman or San-J Tamari
Always buy. Kikkoman for general use. San-J Tamari for gluten-free and richer flavor. Do not attempt to make soy sauce at home.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Fish Sauce
🛒 Buy It
Store option
Red Boat 40°N Fish Sauce
Red Boat is the best fish sauce available. Two ingredients: anchovies and salt. Never make fish sauce at home. Always buy Red Boat.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Hoisin Sauce
🛒 Buy It
Store option
Lee Kum Kee Hoisin
Hoisin is a fermented paste — making it at home doesn't produce the same thing. Lee Kum Kee is the standard.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Gochujang
🛒 Buy It
Store option
CJ Haechandle Gochujang
Gochujang is fermented for months. Always buy. CJ brand is what Korean households use. Find it at H Mart or Asian grocery.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Tamarind Paste
🛒 Buy It
Store option
Tamicon Tamarind Concentrate
Tamarind paste from a jar or block is what you want. Making it from scratch from a tamarind block is fine but the jar is faster and just as good.
Buy on Amazon ↗

🐀 Crew Tested · Pork & Smoker

TEXAS SMOKED
PULLED PORK

Central Texas rub — not the sweet sticky stuff. Equal parts kosher salt and cracked black pepper, plus paprika, granulated garlic, granulated onion, and cayenne. Mustard binder, low and slow at 235°F, spritz every hour after the first two. Wrap at 160°F when the bark is set. Pull at 200-205°F. Rest 45 minutes minimum. Then pull it apart and hit it with a little sauce mixed with apple cider vinegar.

⏱ Prep: 30 min
🔥 Smoke: 8-10 hrs at 235°F
🍽️ Serves: 10
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinPork Shoulder / Butt
methodSmoker at 235°F
woodHickory + Apple
pull temp200-205°F
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Texas Style Rub
Kosher salt NOT table salt
½ cup
Ground black pepper
½ cup
Paprika
⅓ cup
Granulated garlic
2 tbsp
Granulated onion
2 tbsp
Cayenne pepper omit if you don't want heat
2 tbsp
Brown sugar optional — can cause bitterness when smoking
2 tbsp
The Cook
Pork shoulder or Boston butt
8-10 lbs
Yellow mustard binder
2 tbsp
Apple juice / apple cider vinegar mix for spritz
1 cup in spritz bottle

How We Make It

1
Trim, bind, and rub

Trim excess fat from the pork shoulder, leaving about ¼ inch on the fat cap. Pat dry with paper towels. Apply a thin coat of yellow mustard as a binder — just enough to make the rub stick. Combine all rub ingredients and coat the pork liberally on all sides. You shouldn't be able to see the meat underneath the rub.

2
Smoke at 235°F — no peeking for 2 hours

Preheat the smoker to 235°F with a 50/50 blend of hickory and apple wood. Place the pork fat side up on the grates. Close the smoker and don't open it for the first 2 hours. Every time you open it you lose heat and smoke. After 2 hours, spritz with the apple juice/vinegar mix every 45 to 60 minutes.

3
Check the bark, then wrap at ~160°F

Around the 4 to 5 hour mark, the internal temperature will approach 160°F — this is the stall. Before wrapping, verify the bark is set by scraping gently with a finger. If it doesn't rub off, wrap tightly in pink butcher paper or double-layered aluminum foil. Spritz one more time before wrapping. Return to the smoker at 235°F.

// Butcher paper gives better bark. Foil is faster and works fine if you're behind schedule. Either is correct.
4
Pull at 200-205°F — probe tender

At the 7 to 8 hour mark, start probing. The internal temperature needs to reach 200-205°F AND the probe needs to slide in and out like warm butter with zero resistance. Temperature alone isn't enough — tenderness is the real test. When probe-tender, pull it off the smoker.

5
Rest minimum 45 minutes, then pull

Keep it wrapped and let it rest for 45 to 60 minutes before pulling. This is not negotiable — the juices redistribute during the rest. Pull the bone out cleanly, then pull the meat apart by hand or with pulling claws. Mix in a little BBQ sauce combined with apple cider vinegar and a hit of the rub seasoning. Serve on a bun with pickles.

Quick Info
smoker temp235°F
total time8-10 hrs
pull temp200-205°F
serves10
Crew Notes

1.5 hours per pound at 235°F is the planning estimate. A 10 lb shoulder = roughly 15 hours, but timing varies. Use a wireless probe thermometer and cook to temperature, not time. Leftovers freeze for 6 months. Serve with the crew's Texas BBQ sauce.

🐀 Crew Tested · Chicken & Thai-Inspired

COCONUT LIME
CILANTRO
GRILLED CHICKEN

Everything goes in the blender — limes, coconut milk, lemongrass paste, jalapeño, garlic, cilantro, parsley, brown sugar, and soy sauce. Half of that sauce goes over the chicken as a marinade. The other half gets served over the top. Marinate 30 minutes, grill until charred, serve over rice. The sauce is bright, herby, and slightly spicy. The crew doubles it every time.

⏱ Marinate: 30 min
🔥 Grill: 12 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs
methodGrill / Grill Pan
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce (blended)
Limes zest and juice
3 limes (~¼ cup juice)
Low-sodium soy sauce optional
2 tbsp
Full-fat coconut milk
½ cup
Light brown sugar
1 tbsp
Lemongrass paste
1 tbsp
Jalapeño ribs and seeds removed
½
Garlic clove
1
Fresh cilantro
1 small bunch
Fresh Italian parsley
½ small bunch
The Chicken
Boneless skinless chicken thighs
1-2 lbs
White rice cooked according to package
1½ cups uncooked

How We Make It

1
Blend the sauce

Add all sauce ingredients to a food processor or blender. Pulse until smooth. Taste and adjust — more lime for brightness, more jalapeño for heat, more brown sugar to balance. The sauce should be bright green and intensely flavored.

2
Marinate the chicken

Pour half the sauce over the chicken thighs. Toss to coat every piece. Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature while the rice cooks. Reserve the other half of the sauce — this goes on top at serving.

3
Grill until charred and cooked through

Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Grill the chicken for 4 to 6 minutes per side until browned and charred in spots, and internal temperature reaches 165°F. Let rest 3 minutes before slicing.

// Don't move the chicken constantly — let it sit and build char before flipping. Char on coconut marinade is a good thing.
4
Serve over rice with remaining sauce

Plate the rice, top with sliced grilled chicken, and drizzle the reserved half of the sauce over everything. Serve with black beans if you have them. The crew doubles the sauce and uses it on everything.

Quick Info
marinate30 min
grill12 min
serves4
Crew Notes

Lemongrass paste is in the international aisle or the refrigerated herb section. Fresh lemongrass works — use just the pale lower portion, very finely minced. The sauce also works as a marinade for shrimp and salmon. Stores 3 days in the fridge.

SOURDOUGH
ENGLISH
MUFFINS

Active sourdough starter, water, milk, honey, olive oil, flour, salt. Mix the night before. Fold the dough twice over 3 hours the next day. Roll to ½ inch, cut out rounds, cook on a 350°F griddle until firm. Do not cut them open until completely cool — they look doughy but they're done. Fork-split when cooled. Toast them. The nooks and crannies are real.

🌙 Mix night before
⏱ Active: 4+ hrs
🍽️ Makes: 24
🐀 Quick Stats
typeEnglish Muffins
methodGriddle · 350°F
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
Active sourdough starter recently fed and bubbly
1 cup
Warm water
¾ cup
Whole milk warmed
1 cup
White flour bread or all-purpose
5 cups
Olive oil
¼ cup
Honey
¼ cup
Salt
2 tsp
Cornmeal for dusting
for dusting

How We Make It

1
Mix base and autolyse 30 min

Combine water, milk, sourdough starter, and 2 cups of flour in a mixer. Mix until combined. Cover with a towel and let sit for 30 minutes. This autolyse period lets the flour hydrate before kneading and makes the dough easier to work with.

2
Add remaining ingredients and knead

After 30 minutes, add honey, olive oil, salt, and the remaining flour one cup at a time, mixing as you go. Once it all comes together, knead for 3 to 5 minutes until the dough is soft, smooth, and slightly springy. Coat with a small amount of oil, place in a large bowl, cover, and leave in a warm spot.

3
Fold twice over 3 hours

After 1 hour: uncover, reach under one corner of the dough, pull it up and fold it into the center. Repeat around the whole ball (4 folds). Cover and wait another hour. Repeat the same fold sequence after the second hour. Cover and wait another 1.5 hours. The dough should double in size and feel light and springy when done.

4
Roll, cut, and cook on griddle

Dust the counter with flour and cornmeal. Roll the dough to ½ inch thick. Use a round cutter (biscuit cutter, cookie cutter, or glass rim) to cut out rounds. Gather scraps, knead briefly, and cut more — you should get about 24. Dust a baking sheet with cornmeal and rest the muffins on it. Preheat griddle to 350 to 375°F. Cook muffins for 4 to 5 minutes until the bottom browns. Flip, press gently with a spatula, and cook another 2 to 3 minutes. Flip once or twice more as needed to ensure even browning. They should feel firm when pressed, not soft and springy.

// They will look doughy when you pull them off the griddle. Don't cut them open while hot — the interior finishes steaming as they cool on a rack. Wait until completely cool, then fork-split.
Quick Info
active4+ hrs total
griddle temp350-375°F
makes~24
Crew Notes

Always fork-split, never knife-cut. A knife gives you a smooth interior — a fork tears it open and creates the actual nooks and crannies. Store in a bread bag for 3 to 4 days or freeze. Toast before eating. The crew makes these for breakfast sandwiches with eggs and cheese.

GREEN CHILI
CHICKEN DIP

Whipped cream cheese, Greek yogurt, hatch green chiles, pepper jack, jalapeño, cilantro, corn. Season the chicken with tequila lime habanero seasoning and adobo. Combine everything warm and serve immediately with chips. This is the dip the crew makes when there's a crowd and nobody wants to cook a full meal. It disappears in under 20 minutes.

⏱ 20 min
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
typeDip / Appetizer
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dip

8 oz

How We Make It

1
Season and cook the chicken

Season chicken thighs or breasts generously with tequila lime habanero seasoning and adobo. Cook in a pan, oven, or on the grill until done, then shred. Rotisserie chicken works perfectly as a shortcut — just season the shredded meat directly.

2
Mix the dip

In a large bowl or directly in a cast iron skillet, combine whipped cream cheese and Greek yogurt until smooth. Fold in the drained hatch green chiles, shredded chicken, pepper jack cheese, diced jalapeño, cilantro, and corn. Mix until everything is evenly distributed.

3
Warm and serve

Transfer to a cast iron skillet or oven-safe baking dish. Bake at 375°F for 15 to 20 minutes until hot, bubbly, and the cheese on top is melted and slightly golden. Serve immediately with tortilla chips. This dip goes cold fast — eat it hot.

Crew Notes

Rotisserie chicken shortcut saves 20 minutes. Use a cast iron so it stays warm longer at the table. Can also be served as a filling for quesadillas, stuffed in burritos, or spooned over rice. The crew doubles the green chiles for extra heat.

🐀 Crew Tested · Beef & Comfort

SHEPHERD'S
PIE

The crew's version uses sliced roasted potatoes instead of mashed — more texture, more crunch, less effort. Ground beef with onion, garlic, tomato, nutmeg, oregano, paprika on the bottom. A simple béchamel layer goes over the meat. Sliced potatoes on top, shredded cheese over everything, baked in cast iron at 350°F for 30 minutes. Comfort food that doesn't take two hours.

⏱ Prep: 30 min
🔥 Bake: 30 min at 350°F
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinGround Beef
methodCast Iron Oven
difficultyMedium
crew rating8.9 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Meat Layer
Ground beef or half beef / half lamb
300g
Small onion chopped
1
Garlic clove minced
1
Tomato purée or crushed tomatoes
150g
Tomato paste / concentrate
3 tsp
Oregano
1 tbsp
Paprika
1 tbsp
Nutmeg pinch, optional
pinch
The Béchamel
Butter
30g
Flour
30g
Milk
375ml
The Top Layer
Large russet potatoes sliced ~0.5 cm thick
3 large
Olive oil for brushing
drizzle
Shredded cheese cheddar or mozzarella
2 cups

How We Make It

1
Roast the potato slices

Preheat oven to 400°F / 200°C. Slice potatoes into 0.5 cm rounds. Spread on a baking sheet, brush with olive oil, and roast for 30 minutes until just tender and starting to color. They'll finish cooking in the pie.

2
Cook the meat

Brown the ground beef in a pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Add the onion and garlic, cook until soft. Stir in tomato purée, tomato paste, oregano, paprika, and nutmeg if using. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the mixture thickens and deepens in color. Season well with salt and pepper.

3
Make the béchamel

In a separate saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add flour and stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes to cook the raw flour taste out. Slowly pour in the milk while whisking, a little at a time to prevent lumps. Continue whisking over medium heat until the sauce thickens into a smooth, pourable béchamel. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg if using.

4
Layer and bake

Drop the oven to 350°F / 175°C. In a large cast iron skillet, layer the meat mixture on the bottom. Pour the béchamel evenly over the top. Arrange the roasted potato slices in overlapping layers over the béchamel. Scatter shredded cheese evenly over the potatoes. Bake for 30 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and golden in spots. Let it rest 5 minutes before serving.

Quick Info
roast potatoes30 min
bake30 min
serves6
Crew Notes

The sliced potato topping is what makes the crew's version different — it's more forgiving than mash and adds texture on top. The lamb version (half ground lamb, half beef) has more depth and is the traditional move. Keeps 3 days in the fridge, reheats well.

🐀 Crew Tested · Seasonal Baking

PUMPKIN
CINNAMON
ROLLS

Pumpkin purée bread dough with cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice. Brown butter filling with brown sugar and warming spices. Heavy cream poured over the risen rolls right before baking — same technique as the regular cinnamon rolls, same result. Maple cinnamon cream cheese glaze on top. The crew's fall project that takes a full morning and is worth every minute.

⏱ Rise: ~1.5 hrs
🔥 Bake: 22-28 min at 350°F
🍽️ Makes: 12
🐀 Quick Stats
typeCinnamon Rolls
temp350°F
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
Warm milk 100-110°F
120g (½ cup)
Active dry yeast
7g (2¼ tsp)
Brown sugar divided
65-70g (⅓ cup)
Large egg + 1 egg yolk
1 + 1 yolk
Pumpkin purée
240g (1 cup)
Melted butter
57g (¼ cup)
Vanilla
1 tsp
Bread flour added as needed
510-540g (4¼-4½ cups)
Salt
1½ tsp
Cinnamon
1½ tsp
Nutmeg
½ tsp
Allspice
¼ tsp
Brown Butter Filling
Butter browned
113g (½ cup)
Brown sugar
200g (1 cup)
Cinnamon
1½ tbsp
Nutmeg
½ tsp
Allspice
¼ tsp
Vanilla + pinch of salt
1 tsp / pinch
Before Baking + Glaze
Heavy cream poured over risen rolls
½ to ¾ cup
Cream cheese softened
113g (4 oz)
Powdered sugar
120g (1 cup)
Pure maple syrup
4 tbsp
Vanilla + cinnamon
1 tsp each
Heavy cream to thin glaze
4-5 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Proof the yeast

Warm milk to 100-110°F. Mix in yeast and 1 tablespoon of the brown sugar. Let sit 5 to 10 minutes until foamy and active. If it doesn't foam, the yeast is dead — start over with fresh yeast.

2
Mix and knead the dough

Add remaining brown sugar, egg, egg yolk, pumpkin purée, melted butter, and vanilla to the yeast mixture. Mix until combined. Add cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt. Gradually add bread flour until a soft, slightly tacky dough forms. Knead until smooth and elastic. Use olive oil on your hands instead of extra flour to avoid a stiff dough. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.

3
Make the brown butter filling

Brown the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, swirling occasionally, until it smells nutty and golden brown specks appear. Pour into a bowl immediately and let cool slightly. Mix in brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, vanilla, and salt until a thick spreadable paste forms.

4
Roll, fill, slice, and second rise

Roll risen dough into a large rectangle. Spread the filling evenly over the dough. Slice into 12 strips and roll each up. Place in a lined baking dish. Cover and let rise again until puffy, about 20 minutes.

5
Pour cream, bake, and glaze

Preheat oven to 350°F. Pour heavy cream evenly over the risen rolls right before baking. Bake 22 to 28 minutes until lightly golden and cooked through but still soft. If they brown too fast, tent with foil. While baking: beat cream cheese smooth, mix in powdered sugar, maple syrup, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt, add heavy cream to desired consistency. Glaze the rolls immediately after pulling from the oven.

Quick Info
rise~1.5 hrs total
bake22-28 min
makes12
Crew Notes

The heavy cream poured over before baking is the key — same technique as the brown butter cinnamon rolls. Makes them extra soft and pillowy. Make ahead: assemble, refrigerate overnight before the second rise, then take out 30 min before baking and proceed from step 5.

🐀 Crew Tested · Chicken & Chili

WHITE
CHICKEN
CHILI

Chicken thighs seared and shredded. Poblano, jalapeño, hatch chiles, garlic — all going into the pot. White beans, homemade salsa verde, chicken broth, roasted corn. Spice blend with cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, chili powder, and Aleppo pepper. Finished with lime zest and Mexican crema. The crew builds this all the way — no shortcuts, no canned chili shortcut. It's one of the most satisfying soups in the vault.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
🔥 Cook: 30 min
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs
methodOne Pot
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Spice Blend (mix first)
Ground cumin
1 tbsp + 1 tsp
Dried oregano Mexican oregano if available
1 tsp
Smoked paprika
1 tsp
Ground coriander
1 tsp
Chili powder
2 tsp
Aleppo pepper
1 tsp
The Chili
Olive oil
1-2 tbsp
Boneless skinless chicken thighs
1 lb
Yellow onion diced
1 medium
Poblano peppers diced
2
Jalapeño seeds removed, diced
1
Roasted hatch chiles or 4 oz can diced green chiles
½ cup
Garlic minced
6-10 cloves
Beer optional, for deglazing
splash
Low-sodium chicken broth
4 cups
Salsa verde
2 cups
White beans canned, drained and rinsed
2 (15 oz) cans
Fire-roasted corn optional
1 cup
Lime zest of ½ and juice of 1
1 lime
Mexican crema room temperature
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Sear the chicken

Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and half the spice blend. Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high. Sear the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Pull out and set aside — it finishes in the broth. This sear builds the flavor base for the entire chili.

2
Build the aromatics

In the same pot, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the poblano, jalapeño, and hatch chiles. Cook 3 to 4 minutes more. Add the garlic and remaining spice blend and cook 1 minute. Deglaze with a splash of beer if using, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom.

3
Add broth, salsa verde, beans, and chicken

Pour in the chicken broth and salsa verde. Add the drained white beans and fire-roasted corn if using. Nestle the seared chicken back in. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

4
Shred, finish, serve

Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Return shredded chicken to the pot. Stir in lime zest and lime juice. Turn off the heat and stir in the Mexican crema — add it at room temperature off the heat or it can separate. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with more crema, avocado, tortilla chips, and fresh cilantro.

Quick Info
prep20 min
cook30 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Aleppo pepper is worth finding — it adds a fruity mild heat different from regular chili powder. Sub regular chili flakes if needed. The salsa verde is the backbone of the flavor — use good jarred or make it fresh. Keeps 5 days refrigerated, freezes for 3 months.

🐀 Crew Tested · Crockpot & Easy

CROCKPOT
ALFREDO
MEATBALLS

Frozen Italian meatballs, jarred Alfredo sauce, sun-dried tomatoes, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, red pepper flakes, Parmesan, milk. Throw it all in. Cook on low for 4 hours. That's the whole recipe. Serve over pasta, rice, egg noodles, or mashed potatoes. The crew makes this when zero effort is available and still needs something that tastes like someone cooked.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
🔥 Cook: 4 hrs on low
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
typeCrockpot
cook time4 hrs low
difficultyEasy
crew rating8.8 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Everything Into the Crockpot
Frozen Italian-style meatballs store-bought or homemade
1½ lbs
Alfredo sauce jarred
15 oz jar
Sun-dried tomatoes drained and chopped
⅓ cup
Parmesan cheese
⅓ cup
Milk
½ cup
Pepper
½ tsp
Dried oregano
½ tsp
Dried thyme
½ tsp
Onion powder
1 tsp
Garlic powder
1 tsp
Smoked paprika
1 tsp
Red pepper flakes
¼ tsp
Dried parsley for garnish
to taste

How We Make It

1
Throw everything in

Add the frozen meatballs to the crockpot. Pour the Alfredo sauce and milk over them. Add the chopped sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, and all the seasonings. Stir briefly to combine. That's the prep.

2
Cook 4 hours on low

Set the crockpot to low and cook for 4 hours. Don't open it every 30 minutes — leave it. The meatballs thaw, heat through, and absorb the sauce. The sauce thickens and picks up all the seasonings. Stir once around the 2-hour mark if you're nearby.

3
Serve over any starch

Serve over pasta, egg noodles, mashed potatoes, rice, or polenta. Garnish with dried parsley and extra Parmesan. The sauce is creamy, slightly smoky from the paprika, and has that sun-dried tomato sweetness running through it. Better than it has any right to be given the effort.

Quick Info
prep5 min
cook4 hrs low
serves6
Crew Notes

The crew's go-to for game days and busy weeknights. The smoked paprika is the upgrade that takes this from basic to actually good. Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Add fresh spinach in the last 20 minutes for some veg. Works on high for 2 hours if you're short on time.

🐀 Crew Tested · Beef & Pasta

SHORT RIB
RAGÙ PASTA

Two cuts of beef — bone-in short ribs AND beef chuck roast. Charred grape tomatoes, classic mirepoix, harissa paste, balsamic vinegar, red wine, beef stock. Into a Dutch oven and the oven at 350°F for 3 to 3.5 hours until fork-tender. Pull the bones, shred every bit of meat back into the sauce. Pappardelle, Pecorino Romano, fresh basil, a drizzle more balsamic to finish. This is the one the crew makes when people come over and nobody leaves hungry.

⏱ Prep: 30 min
🔥 Braise: 3-3.5 hrs
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinShort Rib + Chuck
pastaPappardelle
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Meat
Grape tomatoes
1 lb (454g)
Vegetable oil
2.5 tbsp
Bone-in beef short ribs ~3 ribs
1.5 lbs (681g)
Beef chuck roast cut into 1-inch chunks
1 lb (454g)
Kosher salt and pepper
to taste
The Braise
Large onion very finely minced
1
Carrots peeled and very finely minced
3-4 large
Celery ribs finely minced
4
Garlic very finely chopped
3 cloves
Tomato paste
2 tbsp
Harissa paste optional but don't skip it
2 tbsp
Balsamic vinegar plus more for finishing
2 tbsp
Red wine dry — Cabernet or Malbec
2 cups
Beef stock
2.5 cups
Fresh thyme sprigs
15
Bay leaves
2
The Pasta
Pappardelle or fettuccine
1-2 lbs
Pecorino Romano grated, plus more to finish
1 cup (122g)
Fresh basil leaves roughly torn
1.5 cups

How We Make It

1
Char the tomatoes

Preheat oven to 350°F. Place grape tomatoes on a foil-lined baking sheet. Using a kitchen torch or the broiler on high, char them until the skins peel back and they're lightly blackened. Rub with paper towels to remove skins, then blend until smooth. Set aside.

2
Sear the meat in batches

Set a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat with vegetable oil. Season all meat with salt and pepper. Sear in batches — 2 to 3 minutes per side until all sides are browned. Don't crowd the pan. Remove to a sheet tray and set aside.

3
Build the sauce

Reduce to medium heat. Add onion, carrot, celery, and garlic with a pinch of salt. Sweat until softened, about 2 minutes. Add tomato paste and harissa paste. Stir and cook until darkened slightly, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the charred blended tomatoes and stir to combine.

4
Add liquid, meat, and braise

Increase to high heat. Add red wine, beef stock, and balsamic vinegar. Bring to a boil, then drop to low. Nestle all seared meat back in, bone side down. Tie thyme and bay leaves together with twine and add to the pot — the liquid should come ¾ of the way up the meat. Cover and place in the oven for 3 to 3.5 hours until fork-tender.

// The harissa paste is optional but genuinely makes the sauce. Don't skip it — it adds depth without making it spicy.
5
Shred the meat back in

Remove meat to a bowl. Discard bones, bay leaves, thyme, and gelatinous membrane from the short ribs. Shred everything as finely as possible by hand or with a metal spoon. Fold all shredded meat back into the pot and stir to combine. If the sauce is too dry, add beef stock 2 to 3 tablespoons at a time. Season to taste.

6
Cook pasta and combine

Boil well-salted water and cook pappardelle to al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining. Return pasta to the pot. Add half the ragù (or all of it for 2 lbs pasta) and toss, adding pasta water 1 to 2 tablespoons at a time to emulsify. Stir in Pecorino Romano and basil. Plate, top with more cheese, cracked pepper, and a drizzle of balsamic vinegar.

Quick Info
prep30 min
braise3-3.5 hrs
serves8
Crew Notes

Make the ragù a day ahead — it's genuinely better the next day. The sauce freezes for 3 months. Use half the ragù for 1 lb pasta and freeze the rest for a second meal. Pappardelle is the right call — wide pasta holds the chunky sauce better than thinner shapes.

TURMERIC RICE +
BRAZILIAN BEANS +
SW SALAD

Three recipes that work as a meal together. Turmeric jasmine rice with sautéed onion and garlic. Brazilian black beans with bacon, garlic, and onion in the pressure cooker. Southwest salad with a blended cilantro jalapeño cashew dressing. Add any protein — grilled chicken, grilled steak, shrimp, or just a fried egg on top. The crew plates all three side by side and it works every single time.

⏱ Rice: 25 min
⏱ Beans: 1 hr
⏱ Salad: 25 min
🐀 Quick Stats
type3-Component Meal
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.3 / 10

Component 1: Turmeric Rice

Ingredients
Ingredients
Butter
1 tbsp
Olive oil
1 tbsp
Onion finely diced
¼ cup
Garlic minced
4 cloves
Jasmine rice rinsed until water runs clear
1 cup
Turmeric
1½ tsp
Low-sodium chicken broth
1½ cups
Bay leaf
1
Salt and pepper
to taste
1
Make the rice

Heat butter and olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and garlic and sauté until softened. Add rice and turmeric, stir until combined. Pour in chicken broth and add the bay leaf. Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat, let sit 5 minutes, remove bay leaf, fluff with a fork.

Component 2: Brazilian Black Beans

Ingredients
Dry black beans picked over and rinsed
1 lb
Bacon cut into ½-inch pieces
4 slices
Onion diced
1 small
Garlic pressed or minced
5-6 cloves
Vegetable or chicken broth
4 cups
Water
1 cup
Kosher salt
1 tbsp
Black pepper
½ tsp
2
Make the beans

Heat pressure cooker to medium-high (sauté setting). Cook bacon pieces until lightly browned. Add onion, cook 3 to 4 minutes. Add garlic, stir 30 seconds. Add beans, broth, water, salt, and pepper. Secure lid, cook on HIGH pressure for 40 minutes, then natural release 15 to 20 minutes. Lightly smash some beans against the side of the pot to thicken, season to taste.

// No pressure cooker? Use the slow cooker version — sauté the bacon/onion/garlic first, then add everything to the slow cooker and cook on low 8 hours. Or use the crew's canned black beans recipe for a fast version.

Component 3: SW Salad + Cilantro Jalapeño Cashew Dressing

Salad
Romaine lettuce washed and chopped
1½ lbs
Yellow + orange bell peppers diced
1 each

1½ cups
Red onion thinly sliced
⅔ cup

⅔ cup

2
Cashew Dressing (blended)
Raw cashews
¾ cup
Water
¾ cup
Fresh cilantro packed
½ cup
Lime juice + zest
3 tbsp + 1 tsp zest
Fresh jalapeño stemmed and seeded
1
Onion powder
1 tsp
Pink Himalayan salt
¾ tsp
Cayenne pepper
⅛ tsp

Make the dressing and assemble

Blend all dressing ingredients until smooth. Let sit 5 minutes in the blender, then blend again. Taste and adjust salt. Assemble salad — romaine, beans, bell peppers, tomatoes, onion, radishes, avocado. Drizzle dressing over the top or serve alongside. Store dressing separately if meal prepping.

4
Plate the full meal

Turmeric rice on one side. Brazilian beans ladled over or beside the rice. Southwest salad on the other side. Add grilled chicken, steak, shrimp, or a fried egg on top. The crew runs all three together — it's a complete meal with zero gaps. The dressing is good enough to eat straight with a spoon.

Meal Timing
beansStart first — 1 hr
riceStart 25 min before
saladPrep while beans cook
Crew Notes

The cashew dressing keeps 6 days in the fridge. The beans keep 5 days refrigerated. Make the beans and dressing ahead for fast weeknight assembly. The meal prep version: prep all 3 on Sunday, portion into containers, add rice fresh each day.

🐀 Crew Tested · Breakfast Classics

BUTTERMILK
BREAKFAST
TRIO

Three recipes that belong together: Buttermilk Syrup that takes 10 minutes and makes everything taste better. Sally's Buttermilk Waffles with whipped egg whites for crunch. And fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes from scratch. Make the syrup first, always. It keeps a week in the fridge and goes on all of it.

⏱ Syrup: 10 min
⏱ Waffles: 35 min
⏱ Pancakes: 15 min
🐀 Quick Stats
typeBreakfast Triple
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.2 / 10

Recipe 1: Buttermilk Syrup

Ingredients
Ingredients
Buttermilk
¾ cup
Granulated sugar
1 cup
Unsalted butter
½ cup
Baking soda
½ tsp
Vanilla extract
1 tsp
1
Make the syrup

Combine butter, sugar, and buttermilk in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a full boil, then boil for exactly 1 minute. Remove from heat and whisk in baking soda and vanilla. It will foam up dramatically — that's right. Serve warm. Store refrigerated up to 2 weeks.

// Use a larger pot than you think you need — the baking soda causes it to foam up significantly. Brown sugar works instead of white for a deeper, caramel-like flavor.

Recipe 2: Sally's Buttermilk Waffles

Ingredients
All-purpose flour
219g (1¾ cups)
Baking powder
1½ tsp
Baking soda
1 tsp
Salt
½ tsp
Eggs separated
3 large
Unsalted butter melted and cooled
113g (½ cup)
Granulated sugar
67g (⅓ cup)
Buttermilk real — no substitutes
420ml (1¾ cups)
Pure vanilla extract
1 tsp
2
Make the waffles

Whisk dry ingredients in a large bowl. In another bowl, whisk egg yolks, butter, and sugar, then add buttermilk and vanilla. Pour wet into dry, stir gently until just combined — lumps are fine, do not overmix. Using a hand or stand mixer, whip egg whites to stiff peaks. Gently fold into batter. Cook in preheated waffle maker on medium-high for 4-5 minutes until crisp. Keep warm in a 200°F oven on a wire rack until all done.

// The separated egg whites whipped to stiff peaks is the secret to crunch. Don't skip this step and don't deflate them when folding.

Recipe 3: Buttermilk Pancakes

Ingredients
All-purpose flour
250g (2 cups)
Granulated sugar
3 tbsp
Baking powder
2 tsp
Baking soda
½ tsp
Salt
½ tsp
Buttermilk
530ml (2¼ cups)
Eggs lightly beaten
2 large
Vanilla extract
1 tsp
Unsalted butter melted and cooled
57g (4 tbsp)
3
Make the pancakes

Whisk dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk buttermilk, eggs, and vanilla, then drizzle in melted butter while whisking. Pour wet into dry and fold with a spoon until just combined — do NOT overmix, a few flour streaks is perfect. Heat a non-stick skillet on medium-low, spray with oil. Once hot, pour ½ cup batter per pancake. Cook until edges look set and bubbles burst, then flip and cook 2 more minutes. Serve with buttermilk syrup.

Quick Info
syrup10 min
waffles35 min total
pancakes15 min
Crew Notes

The syrup is the whole game. Make extra and keep it in a jar. The waffles freeze well — toast from frozen. Both waffle and pancake batters can take blueberries, chocolate chips, or bananas added halfway through mixing. Do not overmix either batter or they go flat and dense.

🐀 Crew Tested · Pasta & Spicy

SPICY
VODKA
PASTA

The move that makes this different from every other vodka pasta: gochujang instead of just red pepper flakes. Guanciale rendered crispy, Fresno chilies, thinly sliced garlic, gochujang and tomato paste caramelized together, splash of vodka, heavy cream, rigatoni, pecorino, cold butter to finish. The crew skips the vodka when needed — it still works.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
🔥 Cook: 15 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
pastaRigatoni
heat levelMedium-Hot
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce
Extra virgin olive oil
¼ cup (60ml)
Guanciale cut into ⅛ inch cubes
4 oz (114g)
Red Fresno chilies finely chopped
2
Garlic thinly sliced
5 cloves
Granulated sugar
2.5 tsp (13g)
Gochujang the secret weapon
3 tbsp (48g)
Tomato paste
1 cup (256g)
Vodka crew mod: skip if needed — still great
1 tbsp (15ml)
Water
¼ cup (60ml)
Heavy cream
1.5 cups (360ml)
Dried rigatoni
1 lb (454g)
Pecorino Romano grated
¾ cup (75g)
Unsalted butter cold and cubed
2 tbsp (28g)
Parmigiano Reggiano to finish
to taste

How We Make It

1
Boil pasta water

Fill a 6-quart pot with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Salt aggressively — it should taste close to seawater. This is the only time you season the pasta itself.

2
Render the guanciale

In a wide 5-quart sauté pan, add olive oil and guanciale over medium-low heat. Stir often for 4 to 5 minutes until the guanciale is crispy and browned. Increase heat to medium. Add Fresno chilies and sliced garlic with a pinch of salt. Sauté until fragrant and softened, about 1 minute.

3
Build the sauce

Stir in the sugar. Add gochujang and tomato paste. Cook, stirring frequently, for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture darkens, thickens, and begins to stick to the bottom of the pan. This caramelization is where the depth comes from.

// Add the pasta to the boiling water right now and cook to al dente. You'll need the pasta and pasta water ready at the same time the sauce finishes.
4
Deglaze and cream

Deglaze with vodka and water, scraping up everything stuck to the bottom. Add heavy cream and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then immediately reduce to low and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened. Taste and add salt if needed.

5
Finish in the sauce

Drain the al dente pasta, reserving 1 cup of pasta water. Add pasta to the sauce pot and toss. Turn off the heat. Vigorously stir in the pecorino and cold butter. Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time to help the sauce emulsify and coat every rib of rigatoni. Serve topped with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano and cracked black pepper.

Quick Info
prep15 min
cook15 min
serves4
Crew Notes

Guanciale is cured pork cheek — look for it at Italian delis. Pancetta or thick-cut bacon work as substitutes but lose some depth. The gochujang is the move — it's spicy, sweet, and savory all at once. Don't skip the vodka step unless you need to; it helps cook off acidity. The cold butter stirred in off-heat is what makes the sauce silky.

🐀 Crew Tested · Korean BBQ

LA GALBI
(KOREAN BBQ
SHORT RIBS)

Flanken-cut short ribs in a marinade built around Korean pear — it tenderizes and sweetens without overpowering. Soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, grated onion, mirin, scallions, black pepper. Marinate overnight minimum, 24 hours is best. Grill on high heat 2 to 3 minutes per side until caramelized. Serve with lettuce wraps, ssamjang, and kimchi.

🌙 Marinate: overnight
🔥 Grill: 6 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinBeef Short Ribs
cutFlanken / LA-style
methodGrill / Broil
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Ribs
Cross-cut beef short ribs flanken / LA-style, ~⅓ inch thick
3-4 lbs
The Marinade
Korean / Asian pear grated — or use an apple
½ pear
Garlic minced — about 6 cloves
2 tbsp
Onion grated
½ medium
Fresh ginger minced — about 1 inch chunk
1 tsp
Soy sauce
½ cup
Water
½ cup
Sugar
3-4 tbsp
Honey
2 tbsp
Cooking rice wine mirin or Korean mirim
¼ cup
Sesame oil
2 tbsp
Scallions finely chopped
3
Black pepper
½ tsp
Sesame seeds optional
1 tsp

How We Make It

1
Prep the ribs

Rinse the ribs to wash off bone dust and remove surface blood. Drain well. Optionally soak in cold water for 20 minutes for even cleaner results. Pat dry. Pound the meat lightly with a meat tenderizer or stretch with your hands — this helps tenderize.

2
Make the marinade

Blend the Korean pear, onion, garlic, and ginger together in a blender until smooth. Combine with soy sauce, water, sugar, honey, rice wine, sesame oil, scallions, and pepper. Stir until the sugar dissolves.

// No Korean pear? Use an apple — Fuji or Bosc work well. The pear tenderizes the meat through enzymes. Don't over-marinate beyond 2 days or the texture gets soft.
3
Marinate overnight

Add ribs to the marinade and coat every piece. Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 to 8 hours, overnight for best results, up to 24 hours. Flip the ribs halfway through. The longer they sit, the deeper the flavor.

4
Grill on high heat

Preheat grill to medium-high. Grill short ribs 2 to 3 minutes per side — turn only once. The sugar and fruit in the marinade caramelize fast. You want char on the outside and just-done on the inside. Serve immediately with lettuce leaves, ssamjang or gochujang, and kimchi on the side.

★
Broiler option

Set oven to broil and preheat. Arrange ribs in a single layer on a broiling pan on the top rack, about 6 inches below the broiler. Broil 5 to 6 minutes until slightly charred, flip, cook another 3 to 4 minutes. Watch closely.

Quick Info
marinateovernight (24 hrs best)
cook6 min on grill
serves4
Crew Notes

The flanken cut (LA-style) is the right call — thinner, more surface area, better char. Look for it at H Mart, 99 Ranch, or ask the butcher. The Korean pear is worth finding. Serve with pa muchim (scallion salad) if you have time. Marinated ribs freeze well — freeze in the marinade, thaw overnight, and cook from there.

🐀 Crew Tested · Bakery-Style Baking

RASPBERRY
MUFFINS

Fresh raspberries, lemon zest, vegetable oil AND melted butter — the two-fat combo keeps them moist and flavorful without going heavy. Streusel topping for crunch. Crew mod: sub coconut oil for the vegetable oil, or go all butter and add a tablespoon or two of plain yogurt for extra tenderness. 400°F, 18 to 20 minutes. They look like bakery muffins because they basically are.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
🔥 Bake: 18-20 min at 400°F
🍽️ Makes: 12
🐀 Quick Stats
typeMuffins
temp400°F
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Streusel Topping
All-purpose flour
30g (¼ cup)
Granulated sugar
50g (¼ cup)
Pinch of salt
pinch
Cold butter diced
2 tbsp
The Muffins
All-purpose flour
240g (2 cups)
Granulated sugar
200g (1 cup)
Baking powder
2 tsp
Kosher salt
½ tsp
Whole milk
180ml (¾ cup)
Eggs
2 large
Vegetable oil crew mod: use coconut oil instead
75ml (5 tbsp)
Melted butter crew mod: go all butter + add 1-2 tbsp plain yogurt
45ml (3 tbsp)
Vanilla extract
2 tsp
Lemon zest
1 lemon
Fresh raspberries
1½ cups

How We Make It

1
Make the streusel

In a small bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, and salt. Add the cold diced butter and work it in with your fingers or a pastry cutter until the mixture is very crumbly and no smooth pieces remain. Set aside in the fridge while you make the batter.

2
Make the batter

Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or butter and flour it. In a large bowl, whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. In a separate bowl, whisk milk, eggs, oil, melted butter, vanilla, and lemon zest. Pour the wet into the dry and stir until just combined. Gently fold in the raspberries — don't break them up.

// Do not overmix. Stop stirring the moment you don't see dry flour. Broken raspberries turn the batter purple and the muffins lose texture.
3
Fill and top with streusel

Divide batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups. Sprinkle streusel generously over each one.

4
Bake 18-20 minutes

Bake at 400°F for 18 to 20 minutes until the tops are golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before removing. Best eaten same day but keep in an airtight container up to 3 days.

Quick Info
prep15 min
bake18-20 min
makes12
Crew Notes

Crew mod: replace vegetable oil with coconut oil for a slightly different richness, or go all butter and add 1-2 tbsp plain yogurt for extra tenderness. Frozen raspberries work — no thawing needed. You can swap in blueberries, blackberries, or diced strawberries. Freeze cooled muffins for up to 2 months.

🐀 Crew Tested · Italian-American

CHICKEN
MARSALA

Chicken breast cut into four cutlets, seasoned, dredged in flour, seared golden in olive oil and butter. Pulled out. Cremini mushrooms browned in the same pan. Garlic, marsala wine, heavy cream. Chicken goes back in to finish cooking in the sauce and thicken it up. 30 minutes start to finish. The crew makes this on date nights and busy Tuesdays alike — it doesn't care which one it is.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
🔥 Cook: 20 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinChicken Breast
methodSkillet · 30 min
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken
Large chicken breasts cut in half lengthwise — makes 4 cutlets
2
Salt and pepper
to taste
Garlic powder
¼ tsp
Flour for dredging
enough to coat
Olive oil
1 tbsp
Butter divided
3 tbsp total
The Sauce
Cremini mushrooms sliced fairly thin
8 oz
Garlic clove minced
1 large
Marsala wine semi-sweet or dry — NOT sweet
¾ cup
Heavy cream
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Prep the cutlets

Cut each chicken breast in half lengthwise to make 4 thinner cutlets. Season generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Coat each piece in flour and pat off the excess — the flour creates the crust and thickens the sauce.

2
Sear the chicken

Heat olive oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add the chicken and sear for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown. The chicken doesn't need to be fully cooked here — it finishes in the sauce. Pull out and set aside.

3
Brown the mushrooms

Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and the sliced mushrooms to the same skillet. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are browned. Keep the heat medium-high — don't let them steam.

4
Build the sauce

Add the minced garlic and marsala wine. Let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom. Add the heavy cream, then add the seared chicken back in. Cook for another 4 to 5 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F and the sauce has thickened. Season with extra salt and pepper to taste. Finish with a little chopped parsley if you have it.

// Use semi-dry or dry marsala — not sweet. Serve over pasta, mashed potatoes, or rice with the sauce spooned over everything. The sauce is the whole point.
Quick Info
prep10 min
cook20 min
serves4
Crew Notes

For extra creamy sauce, increase heavy cream to 1 cup. Chicken thighs work too — sear a little longer. Don't freeze this one — the dairy sauce breaks. Keeps 3-4 days in the fridge. Reheat in a saucepan on low, stirring occasionally.

🐀 Crew Tested · Filipino Comfort

FILIPINO
PORK
ADOBO

Pork belly or shoulder seared in batches for a real crust. Onions caramelized properly — don't rush them. Garlic added last. Then soy sauce, white vinegar, fish sauce, brown sugar, chicken stock, bay leaves. Covered for 30 to 35 minutes, then uncovered for another 30 to 35 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to everything. Serve over rice. Better the next day. Always make extra.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
🔥 Cook: 1.5 hrs
🍽️ Serves: 5
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinPork Belly / Shoulder
methodWok / Dutch Oven
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Pork
Pork belly or pork shoulder cut into 1 to 1½ inch chunks
3 lbs
Coarse salt
2 tsp
Avocado or vegetable oil
2 tbsp
Ground black pepper
3 tsp total
The Sauce
Yellow onion peeled and thinly sliced
1 (about 1 cup)
Garlic cloves finely minced
10
Light brown sugar
3 tbsp
Soy sauce
½ cup
White distilled vinegar
½ cup
Fish sauce optional but recommended
2 tsp
Chicken stock
1 cup
Bay leaves
4

How We Make It

1
Season and sear the pork in batches

Toss the pork chunks with salt until evenly coated. Heat oil in a large wok over medium heat until shimmering. Add half the pork in a single layer — don't crowd it. Let it sit untouched for 2 to 3 minutes, then stir fry and season with 1 teaspoon black pepper. Cook until deeply browned on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes. Set aside on a plate and repeat with the remaining pork. Don't rush the sear — the crust is flavor.

2
Caramelize the onions

After the pork is seared, drain off half to two-thirds of the rendered pork fat. Return the pan to medium heat. Add the sliced onions with a pinch of salt and sauté for 5 minutes until lightly browned. Reduce heat to low and cook another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until well caramelized and jammy. Don't rush this — caramelized onions are one of the key layers of flavor in this dish.

3
Add garlic and return the pork

Stir in the minced garlic and cook 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant. Return the pork to the pan. Add the brown sugar and remaining black pepper. Stir and cook for 1 minute.

4
Build the sauce

Pour in the soy sauce, white vinegar, and fish sauce. Let it simmer for 2 minutes to concentrate. Add the chicken stock and bay leaves. Cover the pan and simmer over low to medium heat for 30 to 35 minutes.

// The Filipino flavor profile here is bold — tangy vinegar, salty soy, savory fish sauce. These are big flavors by design. Don't cut the vinegar or the soy — that's the dish.
5
Reduce the sauce uncovered

Remove the lid and continue simmering uncovered for another 30 to 35 minutes until the sauce reduces to a thick, glossy coating that clings to the pork. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve over white rice with extra sauce spooned over the top.

Quick Info
prep20 min
cook1.5 hrs
serves5
Crew Notes

Make this a day ahead — the flavors deepen significantly overnight. Pork shoulder is more forgiving than pork belly and still excellent. Instant pot: sauté function for searing and onions, pressure cook 30 min, natural release 15 min, then reduce uncovered. Freezes for 2 months.

Tags
PorkFilipinoAdoboRice BowlMake AheadCrew Fave

→

→

🐀 Crew Tested · Jamaican Heritage

JAMAICAN
BROWN STEW
CHICKEN

Marinate overnight. That is non-negotiable. Chicken thighs and drumsticks seasoned with Jamaican green seasoning, all-purpose blend, and smoked paprika, left overnight so the flavors settle into the meat. Then seared in brown sugar and oil for that deep golden color. The stew builds from garlic, onion, scotch bonnet, bell pepper, ketchup, thyme, allspice, and chicken stock. Low and slow, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and the chicken falls off the bone. Serve with rice and peas and fried plantain.

🌙 Marinate: overnight
🔥 Cook: 40 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs + Legs
methodStovetop Stew
heatMedium-Hot
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken + Marinade
Chicken thighs + drumsticks skin removed
3-4 lbs
Jamaican Green Seasoning optional but recommended
2-3 tbsp
All-Purpose Blend or make your own — see notes
2 tsp
Smoked paprika
2 tsp
The Brown Stew
Extra virgin olive oil
3 tbsp total
Brown sugar for browning the chicken
2 tbsp
Yellow onion chopped
1
Garlic cloves minced
4
Bell pepper chopped — mini sweet peppers work great
1 medium
Ketchup or sub tomato sauce
½ cup
Scallions crushed
2
Fresh thyme sprigs
4
Fresh ginger minced
½ tsp
Worcestershire sauce
1 tsp
All-Purpose Blend
1 tsp
Sea salt
1 tsp
Ground allspice
½ tsp
Tomatoes chopped
1 cup
Scotch bonnet peppers minced or whole — reduce for less heat
1-3
Chicken stock
4 cups

How We Make It

1
Marinate overnight (non-negotiable)

Clean and rinse the chicken. In a large bowl, combine chicken with green seasoning, all-purpose blend, and smoked paprika. Mix until fully coated. Transfer to a sealed ziplock bag and refrigerate overnight, or at minimum 3 hours. When ready to cook, let sit at room temperature for 15 to 20 minutes first.

// The overnight marinate is where all the depth comes from. Don't skip it. Jamaicans marinate for 1-2 days — the longer the better.
2
Brown the chicken in sugar

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the brown sugar and stir until it semi-dissolves and becomes wet in texture. Add the marinated chicken pieces and sear 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and caramelized. Pull the chicken out and set aside — it finishes in the stew.

3
Build the stew base

In the same pot over medium-high heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Sauté minced garlic, ginger, and onions until fragrant. Add bell peppers, scotch bonnet, and chopped tomatoes. Sauté 1 to 2 minutes until softened. Add the all-purpose blend, allspice, and salt. Stir until combined.

4
Simmer the stew

Pour in chicken stock, Worcestershire sauce, and ketchup. Stir to combine. Bring to a boil for 1 minute, then add the seared chicken, crushed scallions, and thyme sprigs. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is fall-off-the-bone tender. Add more time if needed for the right consistency.

Quick Info
marinateovernight
cook~40 min
serves4
Crew Notes

Homemade all-purpose blend: 1 tsp each sea salt, black pepper, garlic powder, dried oregano, dried thyme, dried parsley. Serve with Jamaican Rice & Peas and fried sweet plantain. Scotch bonnet is very hot — use habanero for a milder sub, or leave out entirely for a mild dish. Leftovers keep 3-4 days and taste better the next day.

🐀 Crew Tested · Jamaican Heritage

JAMAICAN
RICE &
PEAS

It's called "peas" but it's red kidney beans — that's just Jamaica being Jamaica. Basmati rice cooked in full-fat coconut milk with garlic, onion, pimento seeds, scotch bonnet (pierced, not cut), and fresh thyme. Simmer covered 20 to 25 minutes until the rice absorbs everything and goes from rice to something entirely different. The coconut milk is not optional. Serve as the base for every Jamaican plate.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
🔥 Cook: 30 min
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
baseBasmati Rice
beansRed Kidney (the "peas")
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Rice & Peas
Basmati rice or long grain white rice
2 cups
Red kidney beans (2 cans) drained and rinsed — the "peas"
30 oz total
Unsalted butter or vegan butter
3 tbsp
Small onion chopped
1
Garlic cloves minced
3
Fresh thyme sprigs
3-4
Pimento seeds or sub 1 tsp ground allspice
1 tsp
Full-fat coconut milk 14 oz can — not optional
1 can
Water
1 cup
Scotch bonnet pepper pierced with fork/knife — not cut open
1
Sea salt
1 tsp

How We Make It

1
Rinse the rice

Add the rice to a large strainer and wash with cold water 3 to 4 times until the water runs mostly clear. This removes the surface starch so it doesn't go gluggy. Drain well.

2
Sauté aromatics

In a Dutch oven or large pot over medium-high heat, melt the butter. Add the garlic and chopped onion and sauté until fragrant and translucent, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the pimento seeds, water, and coconut milk. Stir to combine and bring to a boil.

3
Add rice, beans, scotch bonnet

Once boiling, stir in the rinsed rice, drained kidney beans, scotch bonnet (just pierced — not cut), thyme sprigs, and salt. Reduce heat to a low simmer. Cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. If the liquid dries out before the rice is tender, add an additional ¼ cup of water and continue cooking covered.

// Pierce the scotch bonnet but don't cut it open — you want the flavor and mild heat from the skin, not the seeds. Too much heat? Leave the pepper whole and remove after cooking.
4
Rest and fluff

Once the rice is fully cooked and tender, remove from heat. Let it rest covered for 5 minutes. Then fluff with a fork. Remove the thyme sprigs and scotch bonnet before serving. Serve alongside Jamaican Brown Stew Chicken, jerk chicken, or fried plantain.

Quick Info
prep10 min
cook30 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Full-fat coconut milk is the whole point — don't use light. Pierce the scotch bonnet rather than cutting it for controlled heat. This dish is naturally gluten-free and can be made dairy-free by swapping butter for vegan butter. Keeps 3-4 days refrigerated. Make a double batch and use as a grain bowl base all week.

🐀 Crew Tested · Mexican Authentic

PORK
CHILE
VERDE

Sear the pork hot and hard for a proper crust. Braise it for 2 to 4 hours with cumin, oregano, and chicken broth. While that's going, make the salsa verde from scratch: broil poblanos, jalapeños, and tomatillos until charred, steam them in a bag, peel, blend with cilantro. Add that sauce to the pot in the final 30 to 45 minutes. The combination of the slow-cooked pork with that fresh, roasted green sauce is what makes this rival any Mexican restaurant.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
🔥 Cook: 2.5 hrs
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinPork Shoulder
methodBraise + Salsa Verde
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Pork Braise
Pork shoulder (or pork loin) fat trimmed, cut into 1 inch pieces
3 lbs
Salt and black pepper
to taste
Vegetable or canola oil
2 tbsp
Yellow onion large, chopped
1
Garlic minced
3 cloves
Ground cumin
½ tbsp
Dried oregano
½ tbsp
Low-sodium chicken broth
2 cups
The Homemade Salsa Verde
Fresh poblano chiles seeded, halved
4
Fresh jalapeños seeded, halved — keep seeds for heat
2
Fresh tomatillos husks removed, halved
1.5 lbs
Fresh cilantro coarsely chopped
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Sear the pork

Season pork pieces on all sides with salt and pepper. Heat a large stock pot or Dutch oven over high heat. Add oil. Once hot, sear the pork in batches until deeply browned on all sides — don't crowd the pan. Remove the pork from the pot. Add a little more oil if needed.

2
Build the braise

Add onion to the pot and sauté until tender. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Stir in cumin and oregano. Return pork to the pot and pour in the chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 2 to 4 hours until the pork is extremely tender and pulls apart easily.

3
Broil the verde

Set oven rack to second-from-top level and set to high broil. Place halved poblanos, jalapeños, and tomatillos cut-side down on a baking sheet. Broil for 7 to 10 minutes until charred and blistered. Immediately put the peppers (not tomatillos) into a plastic bag, seal, and let steam for 5 minutes. Then peel off the outer layer of skin.

// Seeding the jalapeños controls heat. For mild: remove all seeds. For medium-hot: leave seeds in one jalapeño. For hot: leave all seeds in. The charred tomatillos don't need peeling — they blend fine.
4
Blend and finish

Add the peeled peppers, tomatillos, and cilantro to a blender. Purée until smooth with no large chunks. Pour the salsa verde into the pot with the pork and stir to combine. Simmer uncovered for another 30 to 45 minutes, letting everything meld together. Serve in bowls with warm flour tortillas, Mexican rice, and beans.

Quick Info
prep20 min
braise2-4 hrs
serves8
Crew Notes

Make ahead through step 2, refrigerate, then add salsa verde and finish the next day — this is actually better. Chile verde makes incredible tamale filling. Slow cooker version: sear pork on stovetop, transfer to slow cooker with everything except salsa verde, cook low 7-8 hrs, then make and add salsa verde, simmer 30 more min.

🐀 Crew Tested · West African

NIGERIAN
JOLLOF
RICE

From Zena's Kitchen — her mum's recipe, straight from Lagos. Start with a blended base of red bell pepper, vine tomatoes, red onion, scotch bonnet, garlic, and ginger. Fry onion in oil, darken the double-concentrated tomato purée for that caramelized depth, pour in the blended base and reduce it until the oil separates. Add curry powder, thyme, chicken stock cubes, bay leaves, and water. Then the rice goes in. Cover and cook 25 minutes. This is the recipe.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
🔥 Cook: 50 min
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
originNigerian / West African
baseBasmati Rice
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.6 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Blended Base
Red bell pepper cut into small pieces
1 large
Vine tomatoes cut into small pieces
2 medium
Red onion quartered
1
Red scotch bonnet chillies quartered
2
Garlic cloves smashed
3
Fresh ginger peeled and roughly chopped
25g
Water
100ml
The Rice
Vegetable oil
150ml
Red onion finely chopped
1
Double-concentrated tomato purée DeRica brand if you can find it
150g
Curry powder
1 tbsp
Dried thyme
2 tsp
Chicken stock cubes
3
Dried bay leaves
2
Water
600ml
White basmati rice rinsed until water runs clear
600g
Salt and black pepper
to taste

How We Make It

1
Blend the base

Place all the base ingredients — red bell pepper, tomatoes, red onion, scotch bonnets, garlic, ginger, and water — in a blender. Blitz until smooth. Set aside.

2
Build the sauce

Heat the vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped red onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the double-concentrated tomato purée and cook, stirring frequently, until it darkens and deepens in color, 3 to 5 minutes. This is a critical step — don't rush it.

3
Add the blended base and reduce

Pour in the blended base, stir to combine, and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low and partially cover — it will splatter. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces by about a third and the oil begins to separate from the sauce, 12 to 15 minutes.

// The oil separation is your signal the sauce is ready. This is where jollof gets its depth. Don't skip the reduction — undercooked sauce means flat flavor.
4
Season and add water

Stir in the curry powder, thyme, stock cubes, bay leaves, and water. Season generously with salt and pepper. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.

5
Cook the rice

Meanwhile, rinse the basmati rice thoroughly in cold water until the water runs clear. Once the sauce is boiling, add the rinsed rice and stir. As soon as it returns to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 25 minutes without lifting the lid. Let rest 5 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.

Quick Info
prep10 min
cook~50 min
serves8
Crew Notes

Recipe from Zena's Kitchen — her mum's recipe from Lagos. Use DeRica double-concentrated tomato purée if you can find it at an African grocery store — it's the authentic choice. The slight "party jollof" smoke at the bottom of the pot (the socarrat layer, basically) is not burning — it's the goal. Pull it just before it truly burns. Serve alongside Nigerian Brown Stew Chicken, jerk chicken, or fried plantain.

SCOTCHEROOS

No oven. No marshmallows. Just a peanut butter rice krispie base and a chocolate-butterscotch roof. Crew measurements are locked in: 200g Rice Krispie, 200g sugar, 330g corn syrup, 275g peanut butter. Boil sugar and syrup together, pull off heat, stir in peanut butter until smooth, pour over cereal, press into a 9x13 pan. Melt chocolate and butterscotch chips, spread over top. Let set. Cut into bars. Bring these somewhere and become a legend.

⏱ 15 min active
⏱ Set time: 1+ hr
🍽️ Makes 24
🐀 Quick Stats
typeNo-Bake Bar
ovenNone
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients (Crew Measurements)

Ingredients
Rice Krispie Layer
Rice Krispie cereal Crew: 200g
6 cups (200g)
Granulated sugar Crew: 200g
1 cup (200g)
Light corn syrup Crew: 330g
1 cup (330g)
Creamy peanut butter Crew: 275g
1 cup (275g)
Chocolate Layer
Semi-sweet chocolate chips Ghirardelli or Guittard — quality matters
12 oz
Butterscotch chips
12 oz

How We Make It

1
Prep the pan and cereal

Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan or line with parchment paper. Add the rice krispie cereal to a large mixing bowl and set aside.

2
Cook the syrup

In a large saucepan over medium heat, combine the sugar and corn syrup. Bring to a low boil, then immediately remove from heat. Stir in the peanut butter until completely smooth and combined.

// Pull it off heat THE MOMENT it boils — even a few seconds too long makes the bars hard and crunchy instead of soft and chewy. Don't walk away from it.
3
Coat and press

Pour the hot peanut butter mixture over the cereal and stir quickly to coat all of it evenly. Transfer to the prepared pan and press firmly and evenly into an even layer. Use the back of a greased spatula or a piece of parchment paper to press it down flat.

4
Melt and top

Add the chocolate chips and butterscotch chips to a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on low power for about 2 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds until melted and smooth. Spread evenly over the rice krispie layer. Allow to cool completely at room temperature before cutting into bars. Don't rush this — if the chocolate is still warm it will smear when you cut.

Crew Measurements
Rice Krispie200g
sugar200g
corn syrup330g
peanut butter275g
Crew Notes

Use high-quality chocolate chips (Ghirardelli, Guittard, or Callebaut) — budget chips don't melt cleanly and can seize. Store in an airtight container at room temp for up to 2 days. Freeze for up to 3 months — thaw completely at room temp before cutting. Add 1 tsp vanilla to the peanut butter mixture for even better flavor.

CREAMY
GARLIC
CHICKEN
PASTA

Season the chicken, sear it in one pan. Pull it out. In the same pan: butter, garlic, diced tomatoes, spinach until wilted. Heavy cream and parmesan whisked in until creamy. Slice the chicken, drain the pasta, toss everything together in the pan. Dinner in 30 minutes, looks like you tried harder than you did. The crew makes this on rotation for exactly this reason.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
🔥 Cook: 20 min
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinChicken Breast
methodOne Pan · 30 min
difficultyEasy

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken
Dry pasta any kind — penne, rigatoni, rotini
10 oz
Boneless skinless chicken breast
1 lb
Garlic powder
1 tsp
Italian seasoning
1 tsp
Paprika
1 tsp
Salt and pepper
to taste

Butter
1 tbsp
Garlic minced — 4 cloves is a start, add more

How We Make It

1
Cook the pasta

Boil pasta al dente according to package directions. Drain and set aside. Reserve ½ cup pasta water in case you need to loosen the sauce later.

2
Sear the chicken

Season both sides of the chicken breasts generously with garlic powder, Italian seasoning, paprika, salt, and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large heavy-duty pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken 5 minutes per side until cooked through. Remove from pan and set aside to rest.

3
Build the sauce

In the same pan, add butter and garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add diced tomatoes and spinach, cook 2 to 3 minutes until the spinach has wilted and tomatoes have softened.

4
Cream and finish

Reduce the heat. Add heavy cream and parmesan cheese. Whisk until fully incorporated and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Drain the pasta and slice the chicken into thin slices or cubes. Return both to the pan, toss to combine, and serve.

// Use freshly shredded parmesan — not the pre-shredded kind. The anti-caking agent prevents it from melting smoothly. Grate it yourself and your sauce will be silky instead of grainy.

Crew Notes

Use chicken thighs for a richer result — just cook a few minutes longer. Works with rotisserie chicken too: skip the sear step and just shred into the sauce. Sun-dried tomatoes instead of fresh for a deeper flavor. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated.

TUSCAN
CHICKEN
PASTA

Same technique as every great chicken pasta, but the sun-dried tomatoes make this one different. Sear seasoned chicken, set it aside. Same pan: garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, heavy cream, parmesan. Toss with pasta and sliced chicken. The concentrated tomato flavor from the sun-dried tomatoes gives the sauce depth you don't get from fresh. One pan, 30 minutes, tastes like it took longer.

⏱ 30 min
🍽️ Serves 6
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired byhalfbakedharvest.com
difficultyEasy

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken
Dry pasta penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti
12-16 oz
Boneless skinless chicken breasts
2 lbs
Italian seasoning

1 tsp

Butter

How We Make It

1
Cook pasta and prep chicken

Boil pasta al dente according to package directions. Reserve ½ cup pasta water before draining. Meanwhile, season chicken with Italian seasoning, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper on both sides.

2
Sear the chicken

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 5 to 6 minutes per side until cooked through and golden. Remove from pan and let rest, then slice thin.

3
Build the sauce

In the same pan, add butter. Once melted, add garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add sun-dried tomatoes and fresh tomatoes. Cook 2 to 3 minutes. Add chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer and let it reduce slightly, 3 to 5 minutes.

// The sun-dried tomatoes are the point of this dish. Don't sub fresh — they have a concentrated, chewy richness that makes the sauce taste completely different from basic cream pasta.
4
Finish and toss

Reduce heat. Add spinach and stir until wilted. Add parmesan and stir until melted and sauce is smooth. Drain pasta, add to the pan along with the sliced chicken. Toss everything to coat. Add a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick. Finish with fresh basil and extra parmesan.

Sun-dried tomatoes in oil are way better than dry-pack — the oil carries extra flavor. Slice the chicken before it goes back in so every piece gets coated. Add a squeeze of lemon at the end for brightness. Leftovers reheat well with a splash of cream or broth to loosen the sauce.

🐀 Crew Tested · Breakfast

KNEADERS
CHUNKY
CINNAMON
FRENCH TOAST

Thick, day-old cinnamon swirl bread soaked in a rich egg custard until every bite is saturated. Pan-fried golden in butter. But the move is the homemade caramel syrup — real butter, brown sugar, cream, vanilla, cooked until it becomes something magical and poured hot over the top. This is the kind of French toast that makes you understand why people wait in line for brunch — the DRC cracked it at home.

⏱ 15 min prep
🔥 30 min cook
🍽️ Serves 8
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bysixsistersstuff.com
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The French Toast
Cinnamon swirl bread thick-sliced, day-old is ideal
1 loaf
Eggs
4 large
Whole milk
⅔ cup
Heavy cream
⅓ cup
Granulated sugar
2 tbsp
Vanilla extract
1 tsp
Ground cinnamon
½ tsp
Butter for cooking
2-3 tbsp
The Caramel Syrup (Make This)
Butter
½ cup
Brown sugar packed
1 cup
Heavy cream
½ cup
Vanilla extract
1 tsp
Pinch of salt
pinch

How We Make It

1
Make the caramel syrup first

In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Add brown sugar and heavy cream. Stir and bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. Remove from heat and add vanilla and salt. Keep warm. This is the most important part of the dish.

2
Make the custard

In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon until fully combined. The custard should be smooth and slightly thick.

3
Soak and cook the bread

Cut the cinnamon swirl bread into thick slices, at least ¾ inch. Dip each slice in the custard and let it soak for 20 to 30 seconds per side — you want full saturation but not falling-apart soggy. Heat butter in a griddle or large pan over medium heat. Cook each slice for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Work in batches and keep finished pieces warm in a 200°F oven.

// Day-old bread soaks better without falling apart. Don't rush the cook time — you want that caramelized crust on both sides before flipping.
4
Serve with caramel syrup

Stack the french toast, pour the warm caramel syrup over top, and serve immediately. Add fresh berries or powdered sugar if you want. The syrup is the whole point.

Quick Info
prep15 min
cook30 min
serves8
Crew Notes

Source: sixsistersstuff.com Chunky Cinnamon French Toast recipe. The caramel syrup keeps for 1 week in the fridge — reheat in the microwave or saucepan. If you can't find cinnamon swirl bread, use thick brioche or Texas toast and add extra cinnamon to the custard. This works as a casserole too: pour custard over bread in a baking dish, refrigerate overnight, bake at 350°F for 45 min.

🐀 Crew Tested · Crew Mods

MAC &
CHEESE
(CREW MOD)

Based on the Preppy Kitchen recipe, which is a proper baked mac with a roux base. But the DRC seasoning stack is what makes this hit different: extra garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika, Slap Ya Mama, and cumin. No bread crumbs — the crew doesn't do breadcrumbs on mac. The cheese sauce coats every piece of pasta and the extra spice gives it depth that basic mac never has.

⏱ 30 min
🔥 Bake: 20 min
🍽️ Serves 8
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bypreppykitchen.com
crew modHeavy Seasoning
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Mac
Elbow macaroni or cavatappi cook al dente
1 lb
Unsalted butter
4 tbsp
All-purpose flour
¼ cup
Whole milk
2 cups
Heavy cream
1 cup
Sharp cheddar freshly grated
2 cups
Gruyere or Fontina freshly grated
1 cup
Salt
1 tsp
🔥 DRC Seasoning Stack (Crew Mods)
Garlic powder more than the recipe says
1½ tsp
Onion powder
1 tsp
Cayenne pepper
½ tsp
Paprika
1 tsp
Slap Ya Mama seasoning
1 tsp
Ground cumin
½ tsp
Mustard powder
½ tsp

How We Make It

1
Cook pasta and make the roux

Cook the pasta to al dente (it will continue cooking in the oven). Preheat oven to 375°F. In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add flour and whisk constantly for 1 to 2 minutes until the roux is golden and smells slightly nutty — this cooks out the raw flour taste.

2
Build the cheese sauce

Gradually whisk in milk then cream, adding slowly so lumps don't form. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens — about 5 to 7 minutes. Reduce heat to low. Add all the DRC spices (garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika, Slap Ya Mama, cumin, mustard powder) and salt. Stir in both cheeses a handful at a time until fully melted and smooth.

// Grate the cheese yourself — pre-shredded cheese has anti-caking agent that makes the sauce grainy. Fresh cheese melts into pure silk.
3
Combine and bake (or just serve)

Drain the pasta and add it to the cheese sauce. Stir to coat every piece. Transfer to a buttered 9x13 baking dish. Bake at 375°F for 20 minutes until bubbly. No bread crumbs — crew decision, final answer. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

Quick Info
prep20 min
bake20 min at 375°F
serves8
DRC Mods

Crew mods: extra garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika, Slap Ya Mama, cumin. No bread crumbs. Grate all cheese fresh. Cavatappi or shells hold more sauce than elbows. Don't bake if you want it stovetop-creamy — skip the oven and serve straight from the pot.

🐀 Crew Tested · Detroit Style

DETROIT-
STYLE
PIZZA

High-hydration focaccia-style dough cooked in an oiled steel pan until the bottom is crispy and the edges are caramelized cheese. Crew spec: mozzarella AND Monterey Jack cheese. Sauce goes on last — on top of the cheese, not under it. Dough technique: 1 day in the fridge, freeze, thaw covered for 8 hrs on counter, let rest flattened in pan 30-60 min before topping. Use actual Detroit pizza pans — they make a difference.

🌙 Dough: make ahead
🔥 Bake: 15-20 min
🍽️ Serves 6
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bypalapizza / joeats / seriouseats
cheeseMozzarella + Monterey Jack
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
Bread flour higher protein = better structure
600g
Water room temp, ~75-80°F
450ml (75% hydration)
Instant yeast
½ tsp
Salt
2 tsp
Olive oil for the pan — use generously
3-4 tbsp
The Toppings (Crew Spec)
Mozzarella cheese shredded — cover edge to edge
8 oz
Monterey Jack cheese shredded — crew requires both
8 oz
Detroit-style tomato sauce applied AFTER cheese in stripes
1 cup
Pepperoni or toppings of choice
to taste

Crew Dough Process

1
Mix and cold ferment

Mix flour, water, yeast, and salt until combined — no kneading needed. Cover and let rest at room temp for 20 minutes, then do 2 to 3 stretch-and-fold sets, 30 minutes apart. Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours of cold ferment. This slow ferment develops flavor and gluten structure.

2
Freeze the dough (crew method)

After 1 day in the fridge, portion the dough and place in a ziplock bag. Freeze. This is the crew's method — frozen dough can be pulled ahead of time for any pizza session.

3
Thaw and pan the dough

Take dough from freezer, transfer to a covered Tupperware container, and thaw on the counter for 8 hours covered. Oil the Detroit pizza pan generously — this is what makes the crispy bottom. Add the thawed dough, press gently to fit the pan, and let it rest flattened in the pan for 30 to 60 minutes before topping. Don't rush this step.

// Detroit pizza pans from Amazon are worth buying. The steel conducts heat differently than regular baking pans and produces the characteristic caramelized edge.
4
Top and bake

Preheat oven to 500°F (or as high as it goes) for at least 45 minutes. Top the dough with a mix of mozzarella AND Monterey Jack cheese pushed all the way to the edges. Add any toppings. Add the sauce LAST — in two or three stripes across the top over the cheese. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are deep golden and crispy.

Crew Notes

MOZZARELLA AND MONTEREY JACK — not optional, both cheeses required. The Monterey Jack adds a different melt and flavor. Sauce goes on AFTER cheese. Oil the pan heavily — that's what makes the bottom crispy. Let the dough rest in the pan before topping — don't skip it. Get Detroit pizza pans (the blue steel ones from Amazon).
