🐀 Crew Tested · Slow Cooker

CHIPOTLE
BARBACOA

Sear the chuck roast first — always. Then into the slow cooker with chipotle peppers in adobo, garlic, diced onion, cumin, oregano, ground cloves, and bay leaves. The ground cloves are the ingredient Chipotle actually uses and what makes it taste like the real thing — don't skip or reduce them. 8 to 10 hours on low. Shred, toss back in the juices, let it soak. Serve in burritos, tacos, or bowls with cilantro lime rice.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
🔥 Cook: 8-10 hrs low
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
proteinChuck Roast
methodSlow Cooker
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Barbacoa
Beef chuck roast
3 lbs
Cooking oil
2 tbsp
Salt
1 tsp
Black pepper
¼ tsp
Dried leaf oregano not ground
½ tsp
Ground cumin
½ tsp
Ground cloves the secret Chipotle ingredient — don't skip
¼ tsp
Bay leaves
2
Garlic cloves minced
2
Chipotle peppers in adobo minced — from the can
2
Adobo sauce from the chipotle can
1 tbsp
Yellow onion diced
1 cup
Water or beef broth
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Sear the roast

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add oil. When hot, brown the chuck roast on all sides until deeply seared — 2 to 3 minutes per side. Don't skip this step; the sear builds the fond and depth that makes this taste like the real thing.

2
Load the slow cooker

Transfer the seared roast to a 5-quart or larger slow cooker. Sprinkle the roast with salt, oregano, cumin, and ground cloves. Add the bay leaves, minced garlic, diced onion, minced chipotle peppers, and adobo sauce on top. Pour the water or broth around the sides of the roast (not over the top).

// The ground cloves — ¼ tsp only — is what Chipotle actually uses and what makes the flavor authentic. Don't skip it and don't add more than listed.
3
Cook low and slow

Cover and cook on LOW for 8 to 10 hours or HIGH for 5 to 6 hours. Do not open the lid during cooking. The roast is done when it pulls apart easily with two forks.

4
Shred and return

Remove and discard the bay leaves. Transfer the cooked roast to a plate or cutting board and shred with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat. Return the shredded beef to the slow cooker juices and stir to combine. Let it soak for at least 10 minutes before serving. Serve in flour tortillas as burritos, in corn tortillas as tacos, or over cilantro lime rice as burrito bowls.

Quick Info
prep20 min + sear
cook8-10 hrs low
serves8
Crew Notes

Instant Pot: sear in the IP on sauté function, add everything, pressure cook on HIGH for 70 min, natural release 15 min. Shred and soak. Serve with: pico de gallo, guacamole, Monterey Jack cheese (what Chipotle uses), sour cream, cilantro lime rice, and pinto or black beans. Leftovers keep 4 days and reheat great.

🐀 Crew Tested · Italian Classic

BOLOGNESE

Based on abeautifulplate.com — which follows the Marcella Hazan method, the only method that matters. The secret is whole milk, not cream. And time — 2 to 3 hours of low simmering. Soffritto of onion, celery, carrot. Ground beef and pork browned hard. White wine cooked off. Whole milk added next and simmered away. Then tomato paste and crushed San Marzanos. Then patience. Serve on tagliatelle or rigatoni with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
🔥 Simmer: 2-3 hrs
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired byabeautifulplate.com
methodLow & Slow Braise
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Ragù
Extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp
Unsalted butter
2 tbsp
Yellow onion finely diced
1 medium
Celery finely diced
2 stalks
Carrots finely diced
2 medium
Garlic minced
4 cloves
Ground beef 80/20
¾ lb
Ground pork
¾ lb
Kosher salt + black pepper
to taste
Dry white wine pinot grigio works well
1 cup
Whole milk NOT cream — Marcella's rule
1 cup
Tomato paste
2 tbsp
San Marzano crushed tomatoes
1 can (28 oz)
Fresh thyme or bay leaf
few sprigs
Tagliatelle or rigatoni to serve
1 lb
Parmigiano Reggiano freshly grated, to serve
generous amount

How We Make It

1
Build the soffritto

Heat olive oil and butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion, celery, and carrot. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes until softened and translucent — don't rush this. Add garlic and cook 1 more minute.

2
Brown the meat hard

Increase heat to medium-high. Add the beef and pork. Season with salt and pepper. Break up with a wooden spoon and cook, stirring occasionally, until deeply browned — 8 to 10 minutes. Don't stir constantly; let it get color. Pour off excess fat if there's a lot.

3
Add wine, cook off

Add the white wine. Stir and scrape up everything from the bottom. Let it cook until the wine is completely evaporated — about 5 minutes. The sauce should look almost dry at this point.

4
Add milk, cook off

Add the whole milk. Stir and let simmer until fully absorbed and evaporated — another 5 to 8 minutes. This step is Marcella Hazan's move and it's what makes Bolognese taste different from everything else.

// Whole milk, not cream. The milk tenderizes the meat and rounds out acidity. Don't skip it. Don't sub cream.
5
Add tomatoes and simmer low

Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Add the crushed tomatoes and thyme. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to the lowest setting. Simmer uncovered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring every 20 to 30 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too dry. The sauce is done when it's thick, deep red, and the fat has separated slightly on top.

6
Toss with pasta and serve

Cook pasta al dente, reserve 1 cup pasta water. Add pasta directly to the sauce with a ladle of pasta water. Toss vigorously until emulsified. Serve in wide bowls topped with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

Quick Info
simmer2-3 hrs minimum
serves6
Crew Notes

Make a double batch and freeze half — Bolognese freezes perfectly for 3 months. The milk step is not optional. Tagliatelle is the traditional pasta; rigatoni catches more sauce. Pork is what makes this different from a regular meat sauce — don't substitute all beef.

🐀 Crew Tested · French Country

FRENCH
CHICKEN
CASSEROLE

Chicken thighs seared until golden, then braised low and slow in white wine with mushrooms, shallots, garlic, and thyme. The wine reduces into the stock and becomes something silky — not boozy, just deep and savory. Source: cravinghomecooked.com. One of those dishes that tastes like it took all day when the oven did all the work. Serve with crusty bread, mashed potatoes, or egg noodles.

⏱ 30 min + 45 min braise
🍽️ Serves 6
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bycravinghomecooked.com
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Casserole
Bone-in skin-on chicken thighs
6-8 pieces
Salt and black pepper
to taste
Olive oil
2 tbsp
Bacon or pancetta chopped
4 oz
Shallots sliced
4
Garlic minced
4 cloves
Cremini mushrooms quartered
8 oz
Tomato paste
2 tbsp
Dry white wine
1 cup
Chicken broth
1 cup
Fresh thyme
4-5 sprigs
Bay leaves
2
Heavy cream optional — adds richness
¼ cup
Fresh parsley to finish
handful

How We Make It

1
Sear the chicken

Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 5 to 6 minutes until deeply golden and the skin is crispy. Flip and sear another 3 minutes. Remove and set aside. Don't crowd the pan — do in batches if needed.

2
Cook the bacon and aromatics

In the same pot, render the bacon until crispy, 3 to 4 minutes. Add shallots and cook 3 minutes until softened. Add garlic and mushrooms, cook another 3 to 4 minutes until the mushrooms are browned. Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute.

3
Deglaze and braise

Pour in the white wine, scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom. Let it reduce by half, about 3 minutes. Add chicken broth, thyme, and bay leaves. Return chicken thighs to the pot skin-side up, nestled into the liquid. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook over low heat for 35 to 45 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

// Leaving the skin above the liquid rather than submerging it keeps the skin from going soggy. The braise perfumes the meat from the bottom while the top stays golden.
4
Finish the sauce

Remove the chicken. Fish out the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. If the sauce needs thickening, simmer uncovered for a few minutes. Stir in heavy cream if using. Taste and adjust seasoning. Return chicken to the pot. Serve topped with fresh parsley alongside crusty bread, mashed potatoes, or egg noodles.

Quick Info
sear15 min
braise45 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Bone-in thighs are required — they stay moist and add collagen to the braising liquid. Boneless thighs work in a pinch but reduce cook time to 25 min. Keeps 4 days in the fridge and reheats better the next day. The sauce deepens overnight.

🐀 Crew Tested · Korean Braised

KOREAN
BRAISED
SHORT RIBS
(GALBI JJIM)

English-cut short ribs, blanched to clean them, then braised in a sweet-savory Korean sauce for 2 to 3 hours until the meat pulls off the bone. The sauce: soy sauce, sake, mirin, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, gochugaru, and grated Asian pear. Source: smittenkitchen.com. This is a braised dish, not grilled LA Galbi — different cut, different technique, completely different dish. Both live in the vault for a reason.

⏱ Braise: 2.5-3 hrs
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bysmittenkitchen.com
cutEnglish-cut Short Ribs
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Ribs
Beef short ribs English-cut, 2-3 inch pieces
3 lbs
The Braising Sauce
Soy sauce
½ cup
Sake or dry sherry
½ cup
Mirin
¼ cup
Brown sugar
¼ cup
Garlic minced
8 cloves
Fresh ginger grated
2 tbsp
Asian pear or apple grated — tenderizes meat
½
Gochugaru Korean red pepper flakes
1-2 tbsp
Sesame oil
2 tbsp
Water or beef broth
2 cups
Scallions + sesame seeds to serve
to taste

How We Make It

1
Blanch and sear

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add short ribs and blanch for 5 to 7 minutes to remove impurities and blood. Drain and rinse under cold water. Pat dry. Heat oil in a Dutch oven over high heat. Sear ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove and set aside.

2
Build the braising liquid

Whisk together soy sauce, sake, mirin, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, grated pear, gochugaru, and sesame oil. Add to the Dutch oven along with water or broth. Bring to a boil and add the seared short ribs back in — the liquid should come halfway up the sides of the ribs.

3
Braise low and slow

Cover and braise over low heat (or in a 325°F oven) for 2.5 to 3 hours, turning the ribs every hour, until the meat is fall-off-the-bone tender. Remove the ribs. Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. If the sauce needs to be thicker, simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes until glossy.

4
Serve

Return ribs to the sauce or spoon sauce over them. Serve over steamed white rice, topped with sliced scallions and sesame seeds.

Quick Info
braise2.5-3 hrs
serves4
Crew Notes

Make a day ahead — the sauce absorbs deeper into the meat overnight. Skim the fat from the top after refrigerating and the fat layer lifts right off. Instant Pot: pressure cook on HIGH for 45 min, natural release 15 min, then reduce sauce on sauté. This is Galbi Jjim — braised. LA Galbi in this vault is the grilled flanken-cut version. Two different dishes.

🐀 Crew Tested · Vietnamese

LEMONGRASS
CHICKEN

Chicken marinated in pounded lemongrass, fish sauce, garlic, shallots, brown sugar, and black pepper. The lemongrass is the whole point — citrusy, floral, and unmistakable. Source: provecho.bio. Pan-sear or grill until caramelized and slightly charred at the edges. The fish sauce and sugar hit the pan and create this incredible sticky glaze. Serve over jasmine rice with nuoc cham or pickled daikon.

🌙 Marinate: 1-4 hrs
🔥 Cook: 15 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired byprovecho.bio
proteinChicken Thighs
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Marinade
Boneless skinless chicken thighs
2 lbs
Lemongrass stalks bottom 4 inches only, bruised and minced
3-4
Fish sauce
3 tbsp
Garlic minced
5 cloves
Shallots minced
2
Brown sugar
2 tbsp
Black pepper
1 tsp
Sesame oil
1 tbsp
Vegetable oil for cooking
2 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Make the marinade

Pound or blitz lemongrass in a mortar and pestle or food processor until finely broken down — this releases the oils. Combine with fish sauce, garlic, shallots, brown sugar, black pepper, and sesame oil. Toss chicken thighs in the marinade until fully coated. Cover and marinate at least 1 hour, up to 4 hours in the fridge.

// Use only the bottom 4 inches of the lemongrass stalk — the top is woody and fibrous. Peel off the outer layer first, then bruise with the side of a knife before mincing.
2
Cook until caramelized

Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add chicken pieces in a single layer — don't crowd. Cook undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and caramelized on the bottom. Flip and cook another 3 to 4 minutes. The sugar and fish sauce in the marinade will caramelize into a sticky, fragrant glaze.

3
Serve

Slice chicken and serve over jasmine rice. Top with fresh cilantro, sliced chilies, and a squeeze of lime. Serve alongside nuoc cham dipping sauce or pickled daikon and carrots.

Quick Info
marinate1-4 hrs
cook15 min
serves4
Crew Notes

Fresh lemongrass is worth finding — look in Asian grocery stores. Frozen lemongrass works in a pinch. The DRC also has a Lemongrass Beef recipe in the vault (lemongrassbeef) — same technique, different protein. Grill version: high heat grill, 4-5 min per side, char marks are the goal.

🐀 Crew Tested · Korean

KOREAN
FRIED
CHICKEN

The double fry is the entire secret. First fry at lower temp cooks the chicken through. Second fry at high heat creates the shell. Source: kitchensanctuary.com. Chicken coated in a light potato starch batter — not breadcrumbs, not flour, potato starch — then fried twice. Tossed in either sweet-spicy gochujang glaze or soy-garlic sauce. Stays crispy even after it cools down. This is why KFC (Korean) wins every time.

⏱ 1 hr total
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bykitchensanctuary.com
methodDouble-Fried
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken
Chicken wings or drumettes
2 lbs
Salt, pepper, garlic powder
to season
Potato starch NOT cornstarch, NOT flour
1 cup
Baking powder
1 tsp
Cold water
¼ cup
Neutral oil for frying
enough to deep fry
Gochujang Glaze (Option A)
Gochujang
3 tbsp
Soy sauce
2 tbsp
Honey or brown sugar
2 tbsp
Rice vinegar
1 tbsp
Garlic minced
3 cloves
Sesame oil
1 tsp

How We Make It

1
Season and coat

Pat the chicken completely dry — moisture is the enemy of crispy. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Mix potato starch, baking powder, and enough cold water to make a thin batter (thinner than pancake batter). Coat each piece and let it sit on a wire rack for 10 minutes so the coating sets.

// Potato starch is the key — it produces a lighter, crispier shell than flour or cornstarch. Find it at H Mart or any Asian grocery.
2
First fry — 325°F, 8-10 min

Heat oil to 325°F. Fry chicken in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through and lightly golden. Don't crowd the oil. Remove and drain on a wire rack. Let rest 5 minutes. This first fry cooks the chicken all the way through.

3
Second fry — 375°F, 3-4 min

Increase oil temp to 375°F. Fry the chicken again in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden and shatteringly crispy. The second fry drives out remaining moisture and creates the signature KFC shell. Drain on a wire rack.

4
Make glaze and toss

Whisk together all glaze ingredients in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2 minutes until the sauce is glossy and slightly thickened. Toss the hot fried chicken in the glaze until coated. Serve immediately topped with sesame seeds and sliced scallions.

Quick Info
first fry325°F / 8-10 min
second fry375°F / 3-4 min
serves4
Crew Notes

The double fry is non-negotiable — single-fry KFC is not KFC. Potato starch only. The chicken stays crispy for 20-30 minutes after frying even tossed in glaze, which is unheard of for fried chicken. Soy-garlic version: 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp honey, 5 garlic cloves minced, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp sesame oil.

KUNG PAO
CHICKEN

Marinated chicken stir-fried with Sichuan peppercorns, dried red chilies, garlic, ginger, and peanuts in a tangy-sweet-spicy sauce. Source: chilipeppermadness.com. Crew mod: add red and green bell pepper plus celery for texture. The Sichuan peppercorns give the numbing heat (mala) that no other spice can fake — that tongue-tingling sensation is the whole point of this dish. Don't skip them.

⏱ 30 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bychilipeppermadness.com

difficultyEasy

How We Make It

1
Marinate chicken, mix sauce

Toss chicken pieces with soy sauce, rice wine, and cornstarch. Let sit 15 minutes. Whisk together all sauce ingredients and set aside.

2
Bloom the aromatics

Heat a wok over high heat until smoking. Add oil. Add Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies — let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant and the oil is infused. Don't burn them. Add garlic and ginger, stir 20 seconds.

// The Sichuan peppercorns are what make this dish — they create a tingling, numbing sensation called mala that regular black pepper or chili can't replicate. Find them at any Asian grocery.
3
Stir-fry the chicken and veg

Add the marinated chicken. Stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through and slightly charred at the edges. Add bell peppers and celery (crew mods). Stir-fry 2 minutes until just tender-crisp.

4
Add sauce and peanuts

Pour in the sauce and toss everything together. Add scallions and peanuts. Cook 1 more minute until the sauce thickens and coats everything. Serve immediately over steamed white rice.

Quick Info
cook15-20 min
serves4
DRC Mods

Crew adds red + green bell pepper and celery for more texture and volume. The Sichuan peppercorns are non-negotiable — they're what makes this dish. The dried chilies add heat but not the numbing sensation; you need both. Don't eat the whole dried chilies — they're for flavor, not consumption.

🐀 Crew Tested · Bakery Cookies

BROWNED
BUTTER TOFFEE
CHOC CHIP
COOKIES

Source: handletheheat.com. Brown the butter first — everything else follows from that. The browning converts milk solids into hundreds of new flavor compounds. You end up with a cookie that tastes like butter, toffee, caramel, and chocolate all at once. Toffee bits add crunch and another layer of caramel. Rest the dough 24 hours. Thick, chewy centers with slightly crispy edges. Every other chocolate chip cookie feels like a rough draft after you make these.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
🌙 Rest: 24 hrs
🔥 Bake: 11-13 min at 375°F
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired byhandletheheat.com
key techniqueBrown the Butter
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Cookies
Unsalted butter browned — see step 1
227g (2 sticks)
Brown sugar packed
200g (1 cup)
Granulated sugar
100g (½ cup)
Eggs
2 large
Egg yolk extra richness
1
Vanilla extract
2 tsp
All-purpose flour
280g (2¼ cups)
Baking soda
1 tsp
Kosher salt
1½ tsp
Semi-sweet chocolate chips high quality
280g (1½ cups)
Toffee bits Heath or Skor
150g (1 cup)
Flaky sea salt to finish
for topping

How We Make It

1
Brown the butter

In a light-colored saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Keep cooking, swirling often, until the foam subsides and the milk solids at the bottom turn amber brown and smell like toasted nuts — about 5 to 7 minutes. Immediately pour into a large mixing bowl (including all the brown bits — that's the flavor). Let cool 10 minutes.

// Use a light-colored pan so you can see the color change. Dark pans make it hard to tell when the butter is browned vs burned. Pull it the moment it smells nutty.
2
Mix and chill

Whisk both sugars into the browned butter until combined. Add eggs, yolk, and vanilla — whisk until slightly lightened in color, about 1 minute. Fold in flour, baking soda, and salt until just combined. Fold in chocolate chips and toffee bits. Cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours. Don't skip the chill — it develops flavor and helps cookies hold their shape.

3
Bake at 375°F, 11-13 min

Preheat oven to 375°F. Scoop dough into balls (about 60g each) onto parchment-lined baking sheets, spacing 2 inches apart. Bake 11 to 13 minutes until the edges are set and the centers still look slightly underdone — they'll firm up as they cool. Immediately sprinkle with flaky sea salt. Cool on pan 5 minutes before transferring.

Quick Info
chill24 hrs min
bake375°F / 11-13 min
makes~24 large
Crew Notes

Chill the dough 24 to 72 hours for best results — flavor improves significantly. Pull from oven when centers look underdone; carryover cooking finishes them. Flaky sea salt on top is not optional. Freeze portioned dough balls for up to 3 months and bake straight from frozen, adding 2-3 min.

🐀 Crew Tested · Baking

CINNAMON
ROLLS
(CREW FROSTING)

Source: whisperofyum.com. The crew has one modification that matters most: the frosting. 200g powdered sugar, 115g cream cheese, ½ tsp salt, 1 to 2 tbsp heavy cream. The salt ratio cuts the sweetness and makes it taste like actual pastry frosting instead of a sugar glaze. Fluffy enriched dough, cinnamon brown sugar butter filling, rolled tight, sliced thick, second-proofed, baked golden. Frost immediately while hot so the frosting melts into the swirls.

⏱ ~3 hrs with rises
🍽️ Makes: 12
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bywhisperofyum.com
crew modCream Cheese Frosting
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
Whole milk warmed to 110°F
1 cup
Instant yeast
2¼ tsp
Granulated sugar
¼ cup
Unsalted butter softened
6 tbsp
Eggs
2 large
All-purpose flour
4 cups
Salt
1 tsp
The Filling
Unsalted butter softened
6 tbsp
Brown sugar packed
¾ cup
Ground cinnamon
2 tbsp
🔥 Crew Frosting
Powdered sugar
200g
Cream cheese softened
115g
Salt this is the move — don't reduce it
½ tsp
Heavy cream
1-2 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Make and proof the dough

Whisk warm milk, yeast, and sugar in a bowl. Let sit 5 minutes until foamy. Add butter, eggs, and salt. Gradually add flour, mixing until a soft dough forms. Knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.

2
Fill, roll, and slice

Roll dough out on a floured surface into a 16x12 inch rectangle. Spread softened butter evenly over the surface. Mix brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over butter. Roll tightly from the long edge. Slice into 12 even rolls with a sharp knife or unflavored dental floss.

3
Second proof and bake

Place rolls cut-side up in a buttered 9x13 pan. Cover and let rise 45 minutes to 1 hour until puffed. Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden on top and cooked through. Don't overbake — slightly underdone is better than dry.

4
Make the crew frosting and frost hot

Beat cream cheese until smooth. Add powdered sugar, salt, and enough heavy cream to reach spreadable consistency. Beat until fluffy. Frost the rolls immediately out of the oven while still hot — the frosting melts into the swirls and seeps into every layer.

// The ½ tsp salt in the frosting is the crew's move. It cuts sweetness and makes the frosting taste complex instead of just sweet. Don't reduce it.
Crew Frosting
powdered sugar200g
cream cheese115g
salt½ tsp
heavy cream1-2 tbsp
Crew Notes

Make-ahead: assemble rolls in pan, cover tightly and refrigerate overnight before second proof. Morning of: let sit at room temp 1 hr, then bake. Overnight cold proof actually develops better flavor. Freeze baked unfrosted rolls for up to 2 months; thaw and warm before frosting.

🐀 Crew Tested · Mexican

SHREDDED
BEEF
TACOS

Chuck roast slow cooked until it falls apart in a spiced broth with cumin, chili powder, garlic, oregano, and chipotles in adobo. Source: cookinginthemidwest.com. Low and slow, 6 to 8 hours, until the beef shreds with zero effort. Serve in warm corn tortillas with diced white onion, fresh cilantro, sliced radish, and a squeeze of lime. The cooking liquid reduces into a taco sauce you spoon over the top.

⏱ Slow cooker: 6-8 hrs
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bycookinginthemidwest.com
proteinChuck Roast
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Beef
Beef chuck roast
3-4 lbs
Salt and black pepper
to taste
Oil for searing
2 tbsp
Ground cumin
2 tsp
Chili powder
2 tsp
Smoked paprika
1 tsp

6
Chipotle peppers in adobo minced

How We Make It

1
Sear and season

Season the chuck roast generously with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to the slow cooker.

2
Add the flavors and cook

Sprinkle cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and oregano over the roast. Add garlic and minced chipotle peppers around it. Pour in beef broth and squeeze of lime. Cover and cook on LOW 6 to 8 hours until the beef is fall-apart tender.

3
Shred and reduce

Remove the beef and shred with two forks. Return to the slow cooker and stir into the juices. If you want a more concentrated sauce, pour the cooking liquid into a saucepan and reduce over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until slightly thickened, then pour back over the beef.

4
Serve in corn tortillas

Warm corn tortillas in a dry pan or over a gas flame. Spoon shredded beef into each tortilla. Top with diced white onion, fresh cilantro, sliced radish, and a squeeze of lime. Add the reduced cooking sauce over the top.

Quick Info
cook6-8 hrs low
serves8
Crew Notes

Searing the beef before slow cooking is the move — the crust adds depth that you can't get from throwing raw meat in. The reduced cooking liquid spooned over the tacos at the end is what ties it together. This beef also works in burritos, burrito bowls, nachos, and quesadillas.

🐀 Crew Tested · Mexican Side

AUTHENTIC
MEXICAN
RICE

Source: stellanspice.com. The toasting step is the whole game. Long-grain rice toasted in oil until golden before any liquid goes in — that's what gives Mexican rice its nutty, distinct flavor and keeps the grains separate instead of mushy. Blended tomato, garlic, and onion go in with chicken broth. Cover and steam until fluffy. This is what makes rice at Mexican restaurants taste different from every rice you make at home.

⏱ 30 min
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bystellanspice.com
key stepToast the Rice
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Rice
Long-grain white rice rinsed and dried — do NOT use parboiled
2 cups
Vegetable or canola oil
3 tbsp
Roma tomatoes roughly chopped
2
White onion roughly chopped
½
Garlic cloves
3
Chicken broth
2 cups
Tomato sauce
¼ cup
Cumin
½ tsp
Chili powder
½ tsp
Salt
1 tsp
Frozen peas or diced carrots optional
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Blend the tomato base

Add roma tomatoes, onion, and garlic to a blender. Blend until smooth. Set aside.

2
Toast the rice — the whole game

Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the dried rice. Stir constantly for 4 to 6 minutes until the rice turns golden and nutty-smelling. This step is what makes Mexican rice taste like Mexican rice — don't skip it and don't rush it.

// The rice should be fully toasted — medium golden, not just warm. Watch it carefully; it goes from golden to burned quickly at the end. Rinse the rice before, but dry it fully so it toasts instead of steams in the oil.
3
Add liquid and simmer

Add the blended tomato mixture to the toasted rice. Stir and let it cook for 2 minutes — the tomatoes will sizzle and the liquid reduces slightly. Add the chicken broth, tomato sauce, cumin, chili powder, and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover tightly and cook for 18 minutes. No peeking.

4
Fluff and rest

Remove from heat and let sit covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Add peas or carrots if using. Taste and adjust salt. Serve immediately as a side for tacos, burritos, enchiladas, or any Mexican dish.

Quick Info
cook30 min
serves6
Crew Notes

The toasting step changes the flavor profile entirely. Don't use parboiled rice — the coating prevents proper toasting. Use a heavy pot with a tight lid. The 18-minute steam time with no peeking is important — lifting the lid releases steam and results in uneven cooking. Leftovers reheat well with a splash of broth.

BLUEBERRY
MUFFINS

Souplantation-style from onceuponachef.com. Start them at 425°F for 5 minutes to get the crown to rise fast, then drop to 350°F for the remaining bake. The high-temp start is what gives you that domed bakery muffin top. Buttermilk base for tang and tenderness. Blueberries folded in last so they don't bruise. Streusel topping for crunch. Lemon zest in the batter. The muffin is just a vehicle for blueberries and streusel.

🔥 425°F → 350°F method
🍽️ Makes: 12

How We Make It

1
Make the streusel

Combine flour, sugar, and cold butter in a small bowl. Work with your fingers until crumbly. Refrigerate while you make the batter.

2
Mix the batter

Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin. Whisk dry ingredients together. In a separate bowl, whisk buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, vanilla, and lemon zest. Add wet to dry and fold until just combined — stop when you don't see dry flour, don't overmix. Gently fold in the blueberries.

// Overmixing develops gluten and makes the muffins tough. A few flour streaks are fine. The less you stir after adding the blueberries, the better — crushed berries make the muffin purple and mushy.
3
Fill, top with streusel, bake

Fill muffin cups to the top. Sprinkle streusel generously over each. Bake at 425°F for 5 minutes, then reduce temp to 350°F without opening the oven door and bake another 13 to 16 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. The high-temp start drives the crown up fast. Cool in pan 5 minutes before removing.

Quick Info
bake425°F → 350°F
makes12
Crew Notes

The two-temperature bake is the bakery muffin trick — the blast of heat at 425°F sets the exterior quickly and forces the top to dome before the structure sets. Frozen blueberries work — toss in 1 tsp flour before folding in to prevent bleeding. Keep 3 days at room temp or freeze up to 2 months.

🐀 Crew Tested · Dressing / Sauce

TOMATILLO
RANCH
DRESSING

Source: togetherasfamily.com. Blend tomatillos, buttermilk, sour cream, mayo, fresh cilantro, garlic, jalapeño, cumin, lime juice, and a Hidden Valley Ranch packet. Blend until smooth and creamy. This is the sauce that makes the Cafe Rio sweet pork salad the actual hit. Make a double batch. You'll use it on tacos, burrito bowls, salads, grilled chicken, eggs — it goes on everything for a week and you still won't have enough.

⏱ 10 min
🍽️ Serves: 8+
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bytogetherasfamily.com

difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

How We Make It

1
Blend and taste

Add all ingredients to a blender. Blend on high until completely smooth and creamy, about 1 minute. Taste and adjust — more lime for brightness, more jalapeño for heat, more salt if needed. The dressing should be pourable but thick enough to coat.

// The Ranch packet is not optional. It's the secret that ties the whole thing together and gives it that Cafe Rio flavor you can't quite place. Don't sub homemade ranch seasoning — the packet is specifically what makes this taste right.
2
Chill and serve

Pour into a jar or container. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving — the flavors meld and the dressing thickens slightly as it chills. Serve over burrito bowls, sweet pork salads, grilled chicken, tacos, or use as a dip for quesadillas.

Double the recipe — it goes fast. The Ranch packet is what makes it taste authentic. Pairs with: Cafe Rio Sweet Pork (in the vault as carnitas), burrito bowls, shredded chicken tacos, or as a chip dip. Also incredible as a spread on sandwiches. Keeps 1 week refrigerated.

🐀 Crew Tested · Steakhouse Style

STEAKHOUSE
BUTTER
CAKE

Source: cucinabyelena.com. Individual ramekin cakes — not a sheet cake, not a loaf. Butter and cream cheese batter base, then a separate cream cheese layer poured over the top before it goes in the oven. The cream cheese layer sinks into the batter as it bakes and creates that famous gooey center. Serve warm from the ramekin with vanilla ice cream, fresh strawberry sauce, and whipped cream. This is a restaurant finisher at home. The crew saves this one for special occasions.

⏱ 30 min + 25 min bake
🍽️ Serves: 6
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bycucinabyelena.com
vesselIndividual Ramekins
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Cake Batter
Unsalted butter softened
½ cup (1 stick)
Cream cheese softened
4 oz
Granulated sugar
1 cup
Eggs
2 large
Vanilla extract
1 tsp

1½ cups

How We Make It

1
Prep ramekins and oven

Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter 6 ramekins generously, then coat with sugar and tap out the excess. This creates the caramelized edge. Place on a baking sheet.

2
Make the batter

Beat butter, cream cheese, and sugar together until very light and fluffy, 3 to 4 minutes. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla. In a separate bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Add to the butter mixture and stir until just combined.

3
Make the cream cheese layer

Beat cream cheese, egg, sugar, and vanilla together until smooth.

4
Fill ramekins and bake

Divide the cake batter among the ramekins, filling about halfway. Spoon the cream cheese layer over each one. Bake at 350°F for 22 to 25 minutes until the edges are set and golden but the center still has a slight jiggle — like a cheesecake. Don't overbake; the center firms as it cools.

// A slight jiggle in the center at pull time is correct. Overbaking = no gooey center. Pull it when the edges look set and the top has light color.
5
Serve warm

Let the cakes cool for 5 minutes. Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a plate, or serve directly in the ramekin. Top immediately with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, warm strawberry sauce, and whipped cream.

Quick Info
bake350°F / 22-25 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Quick strawberry sauce: 1 cup sliced strawberries + 2 tbsp sugar + 1 tsp lemon juice, simmered 5 min. For a cleaner pull from the ramekin, butter + sugar coat is important. Can be made ahead: bake, cool, refrigerate, then warm at 300°F for 8 min before serving.

🐀 Crew Tested · Dorie Greenspan

WORLD
PEACE
COOKIES

Dorie Greenspan's legendary recipe. Source: doriegreenspan.com. These are not chocolate chip cookies. They're dark chocolate sablés — intensely chocolatey shortbread with Dutch-process cocoa, brown butter, brown sugar, sea salt, and dark chocolate chunks. The name comes from the theory that if you give these to someone who's in a bad mood, world peace becomes possible. The crew confirms this is true. Slice-and-bake log. Refrigerate the dough first.

🌙 Chill: 3 hrs or overnight
🔥 Bake: 12 min at 325°F
🍽️ Makes: 36
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bydoriegreenspan.com
styleSlice-and-Bake Sablé
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.6 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
All-purpose flour
188g (1¼ cups)
Dutch-process cocoa powder not natural cocoa
30g (⅓ cup)
Baking soda
½ tsp
Unsalted butter at room temperature
170g (12 tbsp)
Light brown sugar packed
130g (⅔ cup)
Granulated sugar
50g (¼ cup)
Fleur de sel or flaky sea salt the non-negotiable finish
½ tsp + more for top
Vanilla extract
1 tsp
Dark chocolate 60-70% cacao, roughly chopped into chunks
150g (5 oz)

How We Make It

1
Mix the dough

Sift together flour, cocoa, and baking soda. In a large bowl, beat butter at low speed until smooth. Add both sugars, fleur de sel, and vanilla and beat on medium for 1 minute — don't overbeat. Add the flour mixture and mix on low just until it looks crumbly. Add the chocolate chunks and mix just until the dough comes together.

// Dutch-process cocoa is required — not natural (Hershey's) cocoa. The Dutch-process has a deeper, less acidic chocolate flavor that makes these taste like a real sablé not a basic cookie.
2
Form the log and chill

Divide the dough in half. Roll each half into a log about 1½ inches in diameter. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 3 hours, up to 3 days. Or freeze for up to 2 months.

3
Slice and bake at 325°F

Preheat oven to 325°F. Slice logs into ½-inch rounds and place on parchment-lined baking sheets, spacing 1 inch apart. Sprinkle lightly with extra fleur de sel or flaky salt. Bake for 12 minutes exactly — they will look underdone and barely set. Don't overbake. Cool on the pan 5 minutes then transfer to a rack.

Quick Info
chill3 hrs minimum
bake325°F / 12 min exact
makes~36
Crew Notes

They will look underdone at 12 minutes — that's correct. They firm up as they cool. The sea salt on top is not decoration, it's flavor. Freeze the log and bake straight from frozen — add 2 minutes. These keep 5 days at room temp, which is longer than they last.

BISCOFF
BUTTER
COOKIES

Source: saltandbaker.com. Same no-bake bar technique as Scotcheroos but with Biscoff cookie butter instead of peanut butter. Sugar and corn syrup cooked to a boil, Biscoff stirred in, poured over Rice Krispies, pressed into a pan. White chocolate or vanilla almond bark drizzled on top. The Biscoff (Lotus cookie spread) flavor is that warm spiced speculoos taste — caramel, cinnamon, cardamom — completely different from peanut butter. If you love the Biscoff cookies on Southwest flights, this is for you.

⏱ 20 min + set
🍽️ Makes: 24
🐀 Quick Stats

How We Make It

1
Make the base

Line a 9x13 pan with parchment. Pour cereal into a large bowl. In a saucepan over medium heat, combine sugar and corn syrup. Bring to a full boil, then immediately remove from heat. Stir in Biscoff spread and vanilla until smooth. Pour over cereal and stir to coat. Press firmly and evenly into the pan.

2
Top and set

Melt white chocolate in the microwave on low in 30-second intervals, stirring each time. Spread over the base. Drizzle melted Biscoff over the white chocolate for the marbled look. Let cool completely at room temperature until set, then cut into bars.

Quick Info
cook10 min + set
makes24
Crew Notes

Biscoff spread (Lotus cookie butter) is found at most grocery stores in the peanut butter aisle or at Costco. Can swap with any cookie butter. White chocolate quality matters — same rule as Scotcheroos: use Ghirardelli or Callebaut. Store at room temp 3-4 days or freeze up to 2 months.

MOO SHU
CHICKEN

Source: thewoksoflife.com. Thin-sliced chicken, scrambled eggs, wood ear mushrooms, napa cabbage, shredded carrots, scallions — all stir-fried together and served in thin mandarin pancakes or flour tortillas. The hoisin + sesame oil + oyster sauce combination is what makes it taste like actual moo shu and not just a stir-fry in a tortilla. The wood ear mushrooms are worth finding — they add the distinctive chewy texture that makes moo shu moo shu.

⏱ 30 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats

difficultyEasy

How We Make It

1
Soak mushrooms and marinate chicken

Soak dried wood ear mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes until hydrated. Drain, trim any tough stems, and julienne into thin strips. Meanwhile, toss sliced chicken with soy sauce, rice wine, cornstarch, and sesame oil. Let marinate while you prep everything else.

2
Scramble the eggs

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the beaten eggs and scramble until just set but still slightly wet. Remove to a plate.

3
Stir-fry chicken

Increase to high heat. Add another tablespoon of oil. Add chicken and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through. Remove to plate with eggs.

4
Stir-fry veg and finish

Add remaining oil to wok. Add garlic and ginger, stir 30 seconds. Add wood ear mushrooms and carrots, stir-fry 2 minutes. Add napa cabbage and scallions, stir-fry 1 minute until just wilted. Return chicken and eggs to the wok. Add hoisin, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Toss everything together. Serve immediately with warm mandarin pancakes or flour tortillas, with extra hoisin on the side.

soak20 min (mushrooms)

Dried wood ear mushrooms are at any Asian grocery — they're cheap and last forever. Mandarin pancakes can be found frozen at H Mart; small flour tortillas work in a pinch. Assemble at the table so everyone builds their own. Make it a build-your-own station for a group meal.

🐀 Crew Tested · Queso Dip

ROASTED
POBLANO
QUESO

Source: urbancowgirllife.com. Velveeta and cream cheese base, but the roasted poblano is what makes this queso different from every other velveeta dip you've had. Roast the poblano directly over the flame until charred, peel, dice. Combine with Rotel, jalapeños, cumin, garlic powder, and the two cheeses. Everything melts together in one pot. Serve hot with tortilla chips and a green salsa swirl.

⏱ 20 min
🍽️ Serves: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired byurbancowgirllife.com
methodOne Pot
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Queso
Velveeta cubed
1 lb
Cream cheese cubed
4 oz
Rotel (diced tomatoes + green chiles) 1 can, don't drain
10 oz can

How We Make It

1
Roast the poblano

Place the whole poblano directly over a gas flame, turning with tongs, until charred on all sides — about 5 to 8 minutes. Or broil 4 inches from the heat. Place in a sealed ziplock bag for 5 minutes to steam. Peel off the charred skin, remove seeds and stem, and dice.

// The roasted poblano is what separates this from generic velveeta queso. Don't skip the roasting or sub with canned chiles — the char is the flavor.
2
Melt everything together

In a medium saucepan over medium-low heat, combine Velveeta and cream cheese. Stir frequently as they melt. Add Rotel (with liquid), diced poblano, jalapeños, cumin, and garlic powder. Stir until fully smooth and combined. Add milk if the queso is too thick. Keep warm on lowest setting.

3
Serve with swirl

Pour into a serving bowl or keep in the pot. Serve immediately with tortilla chips. Optional finishing move: spoon green salsa (tomatillo) in the center of the queso and let people swirl it in.

Quick Info
cook20 min
serves8
Crew Notes

Keep in a crockpot on warm for a party. Reheats well on the stovetop — add a splash of milk to loosen. Add cooked chorizo to make it a full meal. The swirl of tomatillo salsa in the center is the finishing move — do it every time.

🐀 Crew Tested · Breakfast Pastry

HOMEMADE
BLUEBERRY
TOASTER PASTRIES

Source: crowdedkitchen.com. Buttery, flaky homemade pastry dough — handles like pie crust, same technique. Blueberry jam or a quick cooked fresh blueberry filling with lemon zest. Sealed into rectangles, baked golden. Topped with vanilla icing and sprinkles. Ten times better than the box version. The crew makes these as a special weekend project. They keep 3 days and reheat in the toaster oven perfectly.

⏱ Chill: 1 hr
🔥 Bake: 350°F / 25 min
🍽️ Makes: 8
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired bycrowdedkitchen.com
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Pastry Dough
All-purpose flour
2½ cups
Granulated sugar
1 tbsp
Salt
1 tsp
Cold unsalted butter cubed
1 cup (2 sticks)
Ice water
6-8 tbsp
Blueberry Filling
Fresh or frozen blueberries
1½ cups
Sugar
3 tbsp
Cornstarch
1 tbsp
Lemon zest + juice
1 lemon
Vanilla Icing
Powdered sugar
1 cup
Milk
2-3 tbsp
Vanilla extract
½ tsp
Sprinkles
because yes

How We Make It

1
Make the pastry dough

In a food processor or large bowl, mix flour, sugar, and salt. Add cold cubed butter and cut in until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with pea-sized butter pieces. Add ice water 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing with a fork until the dough just comes together. Don't overwork. Divide in half, flatten into discs, wrap, and refrigerate at least 1 hour.

2
Make the filling

In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine blueberries, sugar, cornstarch, lemon zest, and juice. Cook, stirring, for 3 to 5 minutes until thickened and jammy. Cool completely.

3
Assemble

Preheat oven to 350°F. Roll each disc out thin on a floured surface. Cut into rectangles (about 3x4 inches). Place 8 rectangles on parchment-lined baking sheets. Spoon 1 tablespoon blueberry filling in the center of each, leaving a ½-inch border. Brush edges with egg wash (1 egg + 1 tbsp water). Top with a second rectangle of dough. Press edges with a fork to seal. Cut a few vents in the top. Brush entire surface with egg wash.

4
Bake and ice

Bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown. Cool completely. Mix powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla to make icing. Spread over cooled pop-tarts and immediately cover with sprinkles. Let icing set 15 minutes before eating.

Quick Info

makes8
Crew Notes

The dough must be cold to stay flaky — if it gets warm while assembling, pop it back in the fridge for 15 min before baking. Sub any jam for blueberry (strawberry, raspberry, etc.). Cool completely before icing — warm pop-tarts make the icing melt off. Reheat in a toaster oven for best results.

🐀 Crew Tested · Mexican

CHICKEN
BURRITOS

Source: joshuaweissman.com. Everything made from scratch: seasoned chicken, Spanish rice, refried beans, pico de gallo, shredded cheese, sour cream. All wrapped in a large flour tortilla and pressed on a griddle to seal and toast the outside. The difference between a good burrito and a great one is in the rice, the beans, and the chicken all being seasoned properly — not one element carrying the others. Josh's recipe builds each component right.

⏱ 45 min
🍽️ Serves: 4
🐀 Quick Stats
inspired byjoshuaweissman.com
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Seasoned Chicken
Boneless skinless chicken thighs
1.5 lbs
Cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, paprika, oregano, salt
1 tsp each
Lime juice + olive oil
2 tbsp each
The Build
Large flour burrito tortillas
4
Spanish rice see Authentic Mexican Rice in vault
2 cups cooked
Refried beans canned or homemade, warmed
1 can
Shredded Mexican cheese blend
1 cup
Sour cream
½ cup
Pico de gallo fresh is the move
1 cup
Guacamole optional
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Season and cook the chicken

Combine all spices, lime juice, and olive oil. Toss chicken thighs in the marinade. Heat a skillet or grill pan over medium-high. Cook chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Rest 5 minutes, then dice or slice into bite-sized pieces.

2
Warm the tortillas

Warm flour tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan for 20 seconds per side until pliable and slightly charred. Don't skip — a cold stiff tortilla tears when you roll it.

3
Build and roll

In the center of each tortilla (leaving 2 inches on each side): layer refried beans, rice, chicken, cheese, sour cream, and pico de gallo. Don't overfill. Fold in the sides, then roll from the bottom up tight. Place seam-side down.

// The fold then roll technique is the key to a burrito that doesn't fall apart. Sides in first, then roll from the bottom. Tight is right.
4
Press on the griddle

Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat. Place each burrito seam-side down and press with a heavy pan or spatula for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and sealed. Flip and toast the other side. Serve immediately with extra pico, guacamole, and salsa.

Quick Info
cook45 min
serves4
Crew Notes

The griddle press at the end is what makes a homemade burrito taste restaurant-quality — it seals the tortilla and crisps the outside. The Authentic Mexican Rice recipe is in this vault. Refried beans: canned Rosarita work fine, or cook from scratch with the Frijoles recipe in the vault.

🐀 Crew Tested · Thai Sauce

PAD THAI
SAUCE
(STANDALONE)

Every Pad Thai failure is a sauce failure. The crew's locked-in standalone sauce recipe: tamarind paste, fish sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, and white sugar. Make this in a large batch and keep it in the fridge for up to two weeks. Use it for Pad Thai (full recipe also in vault) or as a stir-fry sauce base. The tamarind is the flavor foundation — sour, funky, deep. Fish sauce is the salt. The sugars balance. Don't swap or reduce anything.

⏱ 5 min
🍽️ Makes: 4+ servings
🐀 Quick Stats
typeSauce / Condiment
keeps2 weeks fridge
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce (crew recipe)
Tamarind paste the backbone — don't sub
¼ cup
Fish sauce the salt
3 tbsp
Oyster sauce
2 tbsp
Brown sugar
2 tbsp
White sugar
1 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Whisk and taste

Whisk all ingredients together until the sugars dissolve and the sauce is smooth. Taste — it should be sour, savory, slightly sweet, and deeply funky from the tamarind and fish sauce. Adjust: more tamarind for sour, more fish sauce for salt, more sugar if needed. This ratio is the crew's calibrated version — start here and tweak to your taste.

// Tamarind paste concentrate (sold in a jar) and tamarind block (sold in a block you dissolve in water) are different — adjust accordingly. If using block tamarind: dissolve 50g in ¼ cup hot water and use that liquid.
2
Store and use

Store in a jar in the fridge up to 2 weeks. Use 3 to 4 tablespoons per serving of Pad Thai noodles. See the Pad Thai recipe in this vault (recipe ID: padthai) for the full cooking technique — this sauce makes it.

Quick Info
prep5 min
keeps2 weeks in fridge
Crew Notes

Make a double or triple batch — this stores great and means you can do weeknight Pad Thai in under 20 min. The tamarind is non-negotiable. Substituting with lime juice produces something entirely different. Find tamarind paste at any Asian grocery store or online. See the full Pad Thai in this vault for how to use this sauce.
